TONJ'S DISARMAMENT DILEMMA: WHEN THE SOLUTION BECOMES THE PROBLEM

For a community that has buried too many lives, Tonj was promised peace through disarmament. What residents got instead was another militarized operation, another inflated budget, and the same old fear that the gun will only be taken from some, not all.

A Budget for War and Marginalization, Not Peace

Every time disarmament is announced for Tonj, the figures announced are staggering. Millions are requested for logistics, allowances, and deployment. To a civilian who still sleeps with one eye open, the question is unavoidable: Is this operation about collecting guns, or collecting money and targeting some sections within some Counties in Tonj? 
When budgets balloon but the violence continues, citizens stop believing the goal is security.

The Poison of Selectivity

The core failure is selectivity. Sources on the ground consistently report that disarmament sweeps target certain communities and payas, while other areas known to be heavily armed are left alone. 
That is not disarmament. That is punishment. Sources on the ground have already hinted that Gen. Akech Tong Aleu has prepared the ground for his community to, in a diplomatic way, not disarm by handing over guns, while still giving them the ones in store in his village home.

And when people believe the process is being directed to protect political "hot spots" while punishing others, cooperation dies. Communities hide weapons instead of handing them in, because they do not trust the state to protect them afterwards.

Putting the Arsonists in Charge of the Fire Brigade

Perhaps the most damning part of this cycle is who is tasked to lead it. The President has repeatedly assigned senior military commanders with long histories in Tonj’s conflicts to oversee new disarmament drives. 
This is the same approach that has failed for years. You cannot ask commanders associated with past violence to now be the referees of peace. To the people of Tonj, it looks like being told: "The people who burned your house will now guard it."

That message has consequences. It tells citizens that accountability does not exist. It tells them that connections matter more than conduct. And it tells them that the state is not neutral.

Breaking The Cycle

If Juba is serious about Tonj, 3 things must change immediately:

1.  Independent Oversight: Disarmament must be monitored by a civilian-led committee including elders, women, and civil society, not just the army, and must involve all the senior officers from Tonj in the general headquarters.

2.  Transparency: Publish the budget. Publish the disarmament plan area by area. Let people see it is not selective.

3.  Accountability: Any commander or official accused of abuses must be investigated by an independent body, not protected by rank.

In the past years, Dr. Benjamin Bol Mel and Gen. Santino Wol, during his time, as CDF have collectively murdered so many civilians in Tonj in cold blood. Deng Wol was paid not to give an accurate report about the the harmful roles of Bol Mel.

The same thing is repeating itself: both men, Akech and Deng Wol, are currently still on Bol Mel's payroll to continue with the same trick.

Conclusion

Guns did not create Tonj’s problem. Distrust and known Generals did. 
And you cannot disarm a community at gunpoint while re-arming their mistrust of the government. 

Until disarmament is fair, transparent, and led by people the community trusts, it will remain what it is now: an expensive military exercise that punishes the vulnerable and protects the connected.

I Kanybil Noon, take full responsibility for publishing an article regarding the cheque issued to Legit Investment Ltd.

Owner of Legit Investment Ltd.

Emmanuel Tom Maroma.

The founder of Legit Investment Ltd. is a longtime friend (dating back to the early 2000s). We were young teens living in Yei, and later, we moved to Uganda, where we completed both primary and secondary school in Koboko, Uganda.

He completed his O Level in 2007 and finished his A Level at Midland High School in 2009. Later, he went to Sudan in search of opportunities. Fortunately, he moved to Darfur and worked for the African Union Mission in Darfur until 2011, after South Sudan's independence.

He returned to Juba and immediately secured employment, drawing on his experience with an international NGO. 

While working with NGOs, he also established a private business called Legit Investment Ltd.

His company has been involved in logistics and supplies. In 2023, he became interested in a contract advertised by the Ministry of Interior to supply cars, lubricants, and tires.

He also runs a motor garage in Juba, where the Ministry of Interior contracted Legit Investment Ltd to service their vehicles.

Legit Investment Ltd was awarded a contract in 2023, as shown on the invoices.

Unfortunately, obtaining the rightful resources for the work his company delivered has become problematic. The first two cheques issued expired due to what was described as a lack of cash.

As a businessman, he sought a solution to his business stalemate by looking for help to access his money from the bank. A friend of his, Lual, connected him with ED Deng Wal's wife, hoping she could assist if possible.

During several attempts, as we are all aware of our current situation, Madam Fashogi Adieng accidentally posted these documents on her Facebook status, where they were eventually extracted.

Because her husband holds a significant position in the highest office, I assumed the cheque belonged to her, and the documents were sent to me.

After I published it, Emmanuel Tom Maroma called me and claimed the company belongs to him. He asked me to remove the post, but I told him that if I did, people might think I was bribed. I refused to remove it despite being a childhood friend, pending my own investigation.

As an advocate for transparency and legitimate wealth creation, I have no reason to oppose someone I know has been struggling on his own since 2007.

The resources he invested in Legit Investment Ltd are his genuine sweat and effort, and he deserves the support needed for his business to grow.

Therefore, I call on the Ministry of Interior and other well-wishers to provide the necessary assistance to help him secure payment so his business can prosper.

I am also a strong supporter of entrepreneurship, and I am proud that my childhood friend is a reputable entrepreneur.

Finally, I apologize to ED James Deng Wal Achieng, his wife Madam Fashogi Adieng, and my good friend Emmanuel Tom Maroma, whose company was mistakenly mistaken as one of those shady businesses.

Investigative Report: The Assassination Plot Against First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar Teny and Co-Accused

Our investigations have uncovered a recent plot to assassinate First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar Teny and his co-accused from the SPLM-IO. The plan was orchestrated by Dr. Benjamin Bol Mel, aimed to eliminate Dr. Machar and subsequently blame the government of President Salva Kiir. Despite being under house arrest, Dr. Bol Mel is believed to retain significant influence and resources.

The Sources Watchdog Press has investigated indicate that Dr. Bol Mel's motive stems from his declining fortunes. It is believed that the government has identified all his wealth and is taking steps to seize it. Once this process is complete, Bol Mel is expected to be released from house arrest as a private citizen with diminished influence. Fearing this outcome, Bol conspired to assassinate Dr. Machar and implicated the government as a retaliation against President Kiir and frame him for the killing.

Dr. Bol Mel's familiarity with Dr. Machar's case dates back to his tenure as Vice President for the Economic Cluster, during which he was involved in prosecuting Dr. Machar. This prior involvement has provided him with detailed knowledge of the individuals involved in the case, which he used now to plan the assassination.

According to what we discovered, plot involved bribing court guards and police officers to carry out the assassination through contact poisoning. The plan was to place a deadly substance called Dermal Toxins on the seats of Dr. Riek and his co-accused in the court dock. This toxin, when the targets come into contact with it, will trigger biological pathogens such as bacteria or viruses and then cause chemical poisoning by absorbing directly through the skin into the bloodstream. With that, they would be infected and die slowly while in detention or even shortly after they are released later.

However, the plot unravelled when some of the court police officers involved became dissatisfied with the payment arrangements made by Bol's group. Their expectations were not met, prompting them to secretly report the plan to National Security Services. An investigation was launched, leading to the arrest of two court guard police officers, Francis and Majier.

The two suspects provided conflicting accounts during initial interrogations. Francis said that, in the morning before anyone arrived, his senior, Majier, instructed him to allow some members of the government prosecution team, identified as Ajo Ohisa and Deng Achuil Adija, into the court dock where the accused sit, for inspection. According to Francis, the prosecution team would inspect the accused's chairs and pour the poisonous substance on them. Francis added that he refused and disobeyed Majier's order. Majier, however, denied this account, instead he said that Francis was contracted by associates of Bol Mel to assassinate Dr. Machar. Majier also denied any involvement of the government prosecution team.

The conflicting testimonies prompted the matter to reach President Salva Kiir, who ordered the police's Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to take over the investigation from National Security.

Initial findings suggest that an assassination attempt was indeed planned against Dr. Machar and his co-accused. Evidence points to Dr. Bol Mel as the mastermind, while his motive was driven by a desire for revenge against the government and President Kiir's family, especially Adut Salva Kiir, whom he accuses of betraying him and orchestrating the seizure of his assets.

As the investigation continues, authorities are working to uncover the full extent of the plot and identify all individuals involved. The case has raised significant concerns about the safety of Dr. Riek Machar in detention and the implications associated with security and political tensions in the country. We are still investigating, and we shall bring you the full details once we finish the investigation.

Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir is a well-trained officer with strong military values, experience, and skills. He deserves the opportunity and responsibility entrusted to him.

The appointment of Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir as the Commander of the Presidential Guard, known as the Tiger Division, is a good move. The decision should be respected, and instead of criticizing or challenging his appointment simply because of his family background, South Sudanese should give him a fair chance to prove his leadership and capabilities.

South Sudanese should stop looking at Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir only from the angle of being President Kiir's son. Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir has already laid a good foundation through his role in training special forces, contributing to the development of some of the country's most modern and well-trained military units. He is also known for his commitment to mobilizing young recruits and supporting their training and development.

Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir's Role as Commander of the Presidential Guard

Presidential Guards are elite military or security personnel assigned to protect the Head of State, including the President and official residences.

They are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of the President through close protection, risk assessment, intelligence coordination, and emergency response.

In many countries, the Presidential Guard is a specialized unit with advanced training in security protocols, crowd control, rapid response, and ceremonial duties. Their presence is not only a practical measure for ensuring the safety of the Head of State but also a symbol of national authority, discipline, and sovereignty.

For this reason, Maj. Gen. Atem Salva Kiir should be given the opportunity to demonstrate his leadership, military professionalism, and ability to build a disciplined and effective Presidential Guard. Leadership should ultimately be judged by performance, discipline, professionalism, and service to the nation—not merely by family background.

text:
When Gossip Becomes Governance in the Republic of South Sudan

Instead of doing the actual work of protecting the country, the desperate Director General of National Security, Gen. Akech Tong Aleu, has chosen the path of Palace Politics.

Reliable sources close to the Presidency Affairs say Blue House Gen. Akech Tong has turned his office into a rumor mill. His daily briefs are not about arms flows, militia movements, or threats to civilians, but about running down an exiled politician, Hon. Nhial Deng Nhial — not with intelligence, not with evidence, but with talking points designed to please one audience.

His preferred line: calling Hon. Nhial Deng Nhial a “homeless man disconnected from his community.” It is a convenient fiction. It ignores that millions in the diaspora and at home still follow this politician, still debate his positions, and still see him as part of South Sudan’s political history and future. You don’t erase political relevance by repeating a slogan.

But that’s the point. This is not about national security. It is entirely about access. There were additional sayings that DG Akech Tong also went far in suggesting to the President of the Republic that "working on bringing General Paul Malong Awan and his group members is a better business compared to thinking about Nhial Deng Nhial with his toothless Movement."

And it worked. The president of the Republic is said to have responded positively to the negativity. In return, Gen. Akech Tong was promised: “I will groom you to take over Wanhalel” as Zahim.

The same pattern is playing out with Andrew Kuac Mayol. Night after night, meetings are held not to review security threats, but to coordinate attacks on Hon. Nhial Deng Nhial. Both men act as if volume can substitute for record, and as if tearing down a senior statesman can substitute for building institutions. 

The message being sent is clear: in this office, loyalty theater matters more than competence. Gen. Akech Tong appears to believe that controlling an unaccounted budget and having the president’s ear is the same as earning public trust. It is not. Holding a position is not the same as delivering for the people who pay for it.

Let that sink in.

The head of national security is now using state resources to manage political narratives. Not threat assessments. Not reform. Not protecting citizens. Just messaging and patronage.

That is dangerous for two reasons:

1. It corrupts the institution.
When the DG of Security spends his time curating political attacks instead of monitoring real threats, the entire security apparatus becomes an extension of a PR operation. Intelligence gets diverted from protecting the country to monitoring political opponents. Real dangers are deprioritized while citizens are targeted for their views.

2. It insults the public’s intelligence.  
Calling a political opponent “disconnected” does not build a single classroom. It does not pay a teacher. It does not secure a border. It only tells citizens that leadership thinks distraction is a substitute for delivery.

Gen. Akech Tong Aleu should remember: Wanhalel is not a reward for loyalty tests. It is a public trust. And you do not earn trust by undermining others behind closed doors.

A security chief who governs through rumor will govern with rumor, fear, and favors. That is not statecraft. That is survival politics. And the country deserves better.

Last week, Gen. Akech Tong shamelessly brought a Nigerian performer to Tonj Town for a private ceremony, allegedly to “bring luck” and “lock out” Hon. Nhial. Whether you believe it or not you believe in such rituals, the optics are damning. At a time when Tonj needs security, mediation, and services, the head of national security is being linked to personal theatrics instead of public duty. 

This is not new. The same appetite for spectacle over substance cost a former DG of National Security his job, millions of dollars, and nearly his freedom. Institutions do not survive when leaders confuse office with entitlement.

South Sudan needs a security chief who faces real threats, not invented enemies. Until then, gossip will continue to masquerade as governance.

STATEMENT REFUTING THE CLAIM OF SSP 145 BILLION CASH COLLECTION IN AUGUST 2026

The claim that the South Sudan Revenue Authority (SSRA) collected SSP 145 billion in cash from taxpayers in August 2026 requires serious scrutiny and clarification.

If SSP 145 billion had genuinely been collected and was available to the Treasury, such an amount would have been sufficient to cover the entire national monthly salary bill, which is approximately SSP 116 billion. It is therefore necessary to ask a simple question: where is the claimed SSP 145 billion, and why has the Government continued to face difficulties meeting its monthly salary obligations?

Available figures indicate that the Treasury is currently managing salary payments under severe financial constraints. The monthly salary requirement for the army alone is approximately SSP 22 billion. Even with the purported revenue collection, the Government has reportedly been unable to meet the salary obligations of other security institutions, including the police. Indeed, the reported SSP 40 billion in actual collection could not adequately cover these obligations, resulting in salary payments being deferred until subsequent revenue collections are received.

This situation raises serious questions about the credibility of the reported SSP 145 billion figure and the manner in which revenue collections are being accounted for, transferred and utilized.

Revenue performance should not be measured merely by figures announced publicly. The real test of revenue mobilization is whether the money actually reaches the Treasury and translates into improved government services, regular salaries, and the fulfilment of national obligations.

The continued inability to meet basic salary obligations, despite claims of unprecedented revenue collection, demands an independent and transparent reconciliation of the August 2026 collections between SSRA, the Ministry of Finance and Planning, and the Treasury.

CALL FOR ACTION

It is therefore imperative that His Excellency General Salva Kiir Mayardit, President of the Republic of South Sudan, urgently reviews the leadership of the SSRA.

The country needs a competent, credible and accountable Commissioner General capable of mobilizing revenue effectively, strengthening compliance, eliminating leakages, ensuring transparency and, most importantly, ensuring that collected public revenue is properly accounted for and remitted to the Treasury.

South Sudan cannot afford a revenue system in which large collection figures are announced while government institutions remain unable to meet basic obligations such as the payment of salaries.

The priority must be the country, the Treasury and the welfare of public servants—not inflated collection figures.

URGENT APPEAL FOR THE RELIEF OF THE COMMISSIONER GENERAL OF THE SOUTH SUDAN REVENUE AUTHORITY

To:
His Excellency General Salva Kiir Mayardit
President of the Republic of South Sudan
Juba, South Sudan

Subject: URGENT CALL FOR THE RELIEF OF COMMISSIONER GENERAL MUON DENG AJUET AND IMMEDIATE INVESTIGATION INTO THE DECLINE IN REVENUE COLLECTION

Your Excellency,

We respectfully bring to your attention our serious concerns regarding the current state of revenue collection, administration and management within the South Sudan Revenue Authority (SSRA).

Recent public claims of a significant increase in revenue collection do not, in our assessment, reflect the actual situation on the ground. We believe that the reported figures require an immediate independent verification because available collection trends indicate a dramatic decline, particularly between July and August.

Collection reportedly declined from approximately SSP 154 billion in July to less than SSP 40 billion in August, representing an exceptionally sharp reduction. We believe the following factors may have contributed to this decline:

1. Introduction of cash payment arrangements

The introduction of cash payments for taxes and other government charges, instead of relying on established bank-transfer arrangements, has created serious difficulties for businesses and suppliers.

Many suppliers already have funds held within commercial banks but have been unable to access South Sudanese Pound liquidity because of the severe shortage of SSP in circulation, exchange-rate instability and runaway inflation. Requiring taxpayers and suppliers to make additional payments in cash from outside the banking system has reportedly discouraged some suppliers from continuing to bring goods into South Sudan.

This has had a direct effect on trade volumes and, consequently, on customs and domestic revenue collections.

We therefore urge Your Excellency to direct an independent review of the policy and its impact on revenue collection and the supply of essential goods into the country.

2. Concerns regarding the administration of the Nimule border

We further wish to raise serious allegations concerning changes made at the Nimule border.

It is alleged that Commissioner General Muon Deng Ajuet replaced the Assistant Commissioner at Nimule with Gatluak Riek, following the recommendation of Hon.Ezeckial Lol, and that the changes have contributed to weakened revenue administration at the border.

There are also allegations that Gatluak Riek is being used to facilitate financial arrangements intended to support lobbying and political efforts to retain the Commissioner General in his position. It has further been alleged that substantial weekly sums, reportedly between USD.500,000 and USD 1,000,000, are being channelled for this purpose, with an additional alleged payment of approximately USD 100,000 per week connected to maintaining Gatluak at the border.

These are serious allegations which, if established, would constitute a grave abuse of public office and could have significant implications for national revenue.

We therefore do not ask Your Excellency to accept these allegations without evidence. Rather, we urgently request an independent investigation into the financial transactions, personnel changes and revenue performance at Nimule, including the conduct of Ezeckial Lol and Gatluak.

3. Rapid expansion of SSRA without adequate professional capacity

There are also growing concerns regarding the rapid expansion of the SSRA workforce without corresponding investment in professional capacity, training and institutional controls.

When Commissioner General Muon Deng Ajuet assumed office, the SSRA workforce was reportedly approximately 4,500 employees. The number is now said to have increased to approximately 7,000.

The concern is not simply the increase in staff numbers, but whether recruitment and deployment have been based on professional competence, experience and institutional requirements. There are allegations that some appointments have been influenced by personal loyalty and connections rather than qualifications and experience.

One example raised is Chier Ryran, who is reportedly in charge of hospitality within Domestic Tax and is alleged to have a close family relationship with Commissioner General Muon Deng Ajuet. There are allegations that his role has involved negotiating informal arrangements with hotel owners that result in the Government receiving substantially less revenue than what is actually due.

4. Allegations concerning Dembesh Hotel

A particularly serious allegation concerns Dembesh Hotel.

It is alleged that Chier Ryran negotiated an arrangement under which approximately USD 50,000 was provided for sharing among individuals, including the current Domestic Tax Commissioner Angela Aguot, together with the provision of accommodation on the second floor where Angelo Aguot is alleged to have stayed.

It is further alleged that, following this arrangement, the Government received only approximately SSP 15 million in taxes, whereas subsequent audit findings reportedly identified a potential tax liability of approximately SSP 700 million.

If these allegations are substantiated, they would represent a serious loss of public revenue and require immediate disciplinary, financial and criminal investigation.

OUR URGENT APPEAL

Your Excellency, South Sudan is facing severe economic difficulties, including inflation, foreign-exchange shortages, limited liquidity and declining purchasing power. At such a time, the country cannot afford an institution responsible for collecting public revenue to be weakened by allegations of corruption, political interference, inexperienced appointments or poor management.

We therefore respectfully and urgently call upon His Excellency General Salva Kiir Mayardit, President of the Republic of South Sudan, to:

1. Relieve Commissioner General Muon Deng Ajuet from his position pending a comprehensive and independent review of his administration of the SSRA.
2. Appoint a competent, experienced and professionally independent person to lead the Authority and restore public confidence.
3. Order an independent forensic investigation into the SSRA’s revenue collections, expenditure, recruitment, appointments and financial transactions during the tenure of the current Commissioner General.
4. Direct a comprehensive investigation into the Nimule border operations, including the conduct and financial activities of Gatluak Riek.
5. Investigate the allegations involving Chier Ryran and Angelo Aguot, particularly those relating to Dembesh Hotel and other hospitality taxpayers.
6. Review the dramatic increase in SSRA staffing from approximately 4,500 to 7,000 employees, including the recruitment procedures, qualifications and financial implications.
7. Independently verify the publicly reported revenue figures and reconcile them against actual collections, bank records, customs records and taxpayer declarations.
8. Take immediate measures to restore confidence among businesses, suppliers and taxpayers so that revenue collection and the supply of essential goods can recover.

Your Excellency, this appeal is not intended to undermine the institution of the SSRA. On the contrary, it is intended to protect the Authority, safeguard public revenue and prevent further deterioration of the national economy.

The country urgently needs a revenue administration based on professionalism, transparency, accountability and competence. Where allegations of corruption or abuse of office arise, they should be investigated without fear or favour, regardless of the position or connections of the individuals involved.

We therefore make this urgent call for the relief of Commissioner General Muon Deng Ajuet and the immediate commencement of an independent investigation into the matters outlined above.

The economic situation requires decisive action before further revenue losses and institutional damage occur.

Respectfully submitted,

Concerned Citizens and Stakeholders of South Sudan
Juba, South Sudan

THE WATCHDOG PRESS MEDIA RESPONDS: BEFORE YOU LECTURE THE WATCHDOG, EXAMINE YOUR OWN PROFESSIONAL RECORD

We have carefully read the lengthy article published by Simon Machuar Manhkeracnaak, the self-appointed Managing Editor of the R.I.P Agamlong English Daily Newspaper, under the dramatic headline:

“THE WATCHDOG PRESS MEDIA: A COWARDLY NEWS OUTLET HIDING BEHIND SENSATIONALISM.”

At The Watchdog Press Media, we welcome criticism. We do not consider ourselves above scrutiny, and we do not expect every reader, journalist, politician, or media organization to agree with everything we publish.

However, criticism itself must meet a certain standard.

Before one positions himself as the instructor of an established media platform, one must first demonstrate the professional maturity, consistency, experience, independence and institutional credibility necessary to lecture others about journalism.

And this brings us to a very simple but serious question:

What exactly qualifies Simon Machuar Manhkeracnaak to present himself as the authority on professional journalism while his own media project, Agamlong English Daily Newspaper, appears to have disappeared from the public space before demonstrating the longevity and institutional sustainability expected of a serious daily newspaper?

FIRST, LET US DISCUSS PROFESSIONAL MATURITY

Your article repeatedly speaks about “professional journalism,” “verification,” “accountability,” “evidence,” “responsibility,” and “professional courage.”

Those are important principles.

But professional journalism is not demonstrated by writing a long article containing the words evidence, verification, accountability, and responsibility repeatedly.

It is demonstrated through consistent practice.

It is demonstrated through editorial discipline.

It is demonstrated through years of publication.

It is demonstrated through institutional survival.

It is demonstrated through accuracy, corrections, credibility, independence and public trust.

Therefore, before you tell The Watchdog Media how a watchdog should operate, perhaps you should answer a more fundamental question:

Where is the media institution you were managing?

Why did the so-called Agamlong English Daily Newspaper fail to sustain itself as a daily newspaper for even the expected period of two or three consecutive years?

What happened?

Was the problem funding?

Was it management?

Was it readership?

Was it editorial capacity?

Was it professional organization?

Was it political interference?

Was it lack of sustainability?

Or was it simply a failure of institutional planning?

We are not asking these questions to celebrate anybody's failure.

We are asking because you have voluntarily placed your professional credentials on the table by presenting yourself as a Managing Editor qualified to lecture another media organization about journalism.

Once you do that, your own professional record becomes relevant.

You cannot demand that The Watchdog Media answer every question while refusing to answer questions about your own media experience.

YOU WROTE: “WHERE IS THE EVIDENCE?”

Excellent question.

But the same question can be directed back to you:

Where is the evidence of your long-term success as a media manager?

Where is the sustained publication record?

Where is the institutional legacy?

Where is the newsroom you built?

Where is the newspaper that survived under your editorial leadership?

Where is the professional career that gives you the authority to portray yourself as the final referee of journalistic standards?

You cannot selectively apply the principle of accountability.

If evidence matters when The Watchdog Media publishes a story, evidence should also matter when you make sweeping conclusions about The Watchdog Press Media.

You wrote:

“What we are seeing instead risks turning journalism into a political weapon.”

That is a serious accusation.

So we ask you:

What evidence demonstrates that The Watchdog Media is being used as a political weapon?

Which political organization controls it?

Which politician owns it?

Who finances it?

Who dictates its editorial line?

Who provides its instructions?

Who determines what it publishes?

If you are making such a serious characterization, then apply the same standard you demanded from us:

Bring the evidence.

Otherwise, by your own definition, you have merely made an allegation.

YOU ASKED: “WHO WATCHES THE WATCHDOG?”

We appreciate the question.

But perhaps the more appropriate question today is:

Who watches the people claiming to watch the watchdog?

Who evaluates your editorial judgment?

Who evaluates your professional competence?

Who evaluates the sustainability of your media initiatives?

Who examines the reasons behind the disappearance of Agamlong English Daily Newspaper?

Who challenges your own political assumptions?

Who verifies the allegations contained in your lengthy article?

And perhaps the most uncomfortable question:

Who gave you the professional mandate to declare yourself the judge of another media organization's credibility?

We do not fear scrutiny.

But scrutiny must be reciprocal.

If you want to watch the Watchdog Press, then be prepared to be watched yourself.

POLITICAL IDENTITY MATTERS WHEN YOU ATTACK POLITICAL JOURNALISM

Your article repeatedly raises questions about political agendas.

So let us ask you directly:

Who are you politically?

What political interests have you historically associated yourself with?

What political environment shaped your journalism?

What political actors have you worked with?

What political relationships have influenced your understanding of public affairs?

And most importantly:

Can you honestly demonstrate that you approach political reporting from a position completely free of political bias?

We are not saying that having political opinions automatically disqualifies someone from journalism.

It does not.

But if you are going to accuse another media outlet of having a political agenda, you must also be prepared to disclose and defend your own editorial and political positioning.

The public deserves transparency from everyone—not only from those you criticize.

YOU WROTE: “STOP CONFUSING PROPAGANDA WITH JOURNALISM.”

Again, we agree with the principle.

But this principle applies to everyone.

It applies to The Watchdog Press Media.

It applies to Agamlong English Daily Newspaper.

It applies to every journalist.

It applies to every political commentator.

It applies to every social-media publisher.

It applies to every so-called investigative journalist.

Nobody owns journalism.

Nobody has a monopoly on truth.

And certainly nobody becomes the embodiment of professional journalism merely because they can produce a lengthy article criticizing another media outlet.

The real test is simple:

Can your reporting survive scrutiny?

Can your allegations be verified?

Can your conclusions be defended?

Can your sources withstand examination?

Can your editorial decisions be explained?

Can your organization survive beyond the excitement of its launch?

Can you build an institution rather than simply build a title?

Those are the questions that determine professional maturity.

A NEWSPAPER IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY A NAME ALONE

Calling an organization a “Daily Newspaper” does not automatically make it a successful daily newspaper.

Calling oneself “Managing Editor” does not automatically establish decades of editorial experience.

Printing a masthead does not create institutional credibility.

A professional title is earned through performance.

A media institution is built through consistency.

A newspaper earns public confidence through accuracy.

And a journalist earns respect through years of responsible work.

That is why we find it strange that you chose to devote such a long article to instructing The Watchdog Media while leaving your own professional journey largely outside the examination.

You wrote a very long lecture.

But journalism is not an examination where the person holding the pen automatically becomes the professor.

Your own record must also be examined.

AND HERE IS THE QUESTION ABOUT CAREER

You ask us, directly or indirectly, to demonstrate professional standards.

Fine.

But we ask you something equally important:

Who are you in the professional hierarchy of South Sudanese journalism?

Are you among those journalists who have earned an unquestionable career through decades of consistent professional service?

Are you among those who have built media institutions that survived difficult political and economic environments?

Are you among those who have established a respected editorial legacy?

Or are you still trying to establish yourself professionally?

There is nothing shameful about building a career.

Every respected journalist started somewhere.

Every serious media institution started small.

But there is something professionally problematic about attempting to stand on a high moral and professional platform while your own institutional record remains open to serious questions.

The question is not whether you have the right to criticize us.

You absolutely do.

The question is whether you have demonstrated the maturity to criticize without pretending that your own record is beyond examination.

YOU WROTE: “THERE IS NOTHING COURAGEOUS ABOUT PUBLISHING UNVERIFIED ALLEGATIONS.”

Correct.

But there is also nothing courageous about making sweeping accusations against another media organization and then refusing to provide evidence supporting your own characterization.

Calling The Watchdog Media “cowardly” is itself an accusation.

Calling our journalism “propaganda” is an accusation.

Claiming that we manufacture political narratives is an accusation.

Suggesting that we publish hearsay is an accusation.

Therefore, under the very standards you established in your own article:

Where is your evidence?

Where is the investigation proving that we deliberately publish false information?

Where is the evidence proving that our editorial decisions are politically controlled?

Where is the evidence proving that our stories are fabricated?

Where is the evidence proving that we intentionally manufacture narratives?

You cannot demand evidentiary standards from us while lowering those same standards for yourself.

That would be the very hypocrisy you accuse others of practicing.

THE WATCHDOG PRESS MEDIA DOES NOT NEED YOUR PERMISSION TO EXIST OR RUNS ITS MEANINGFUL ACTIVITIES 

Let us make something very clear.

The Watchdog Media does not need permission from any individual journalist to perform its work.

We do not need political approval.

We do not need validation from aspiring media personalities.

We do not need endorsement from individuals whose own media projects have struggled to establish sustainable institutional footprints.

Our responsibility is to our readers.

Our responsibility is to the public interest.

And where we make mistakes, we should be prepared to correct them.

That is what accountability means.

But accountability does not mean surrendering our editorial independence to someone who demands that we publish whatever evidence he personally considers sufficient.

JOURNALISM IS NOT A COMPETITION FOR MORAL SUPERIORITY

Your article is written as though The Watchdog Media must choose between following your instructions and abandoning journalism.

You conclude:

“The Watchdog Press Media should either rise to the standards of professional journalism or stop pretending that sensationalism is investigative reporting.”

We have heard your advice.

But we respectfully reject the assumption that you have been appointed as the supreme regulator of journalism.

You are entitled to your opinion.

You are entitled to criticize us.

You are entitled to challenge our reporting.

But you are not entitled to define yourself as the final authority over our editorial independence.

If you believe one of our stories is inaccurate, identify the story.

If you believe a specific allegation is false, identify the allegation.

If you possess contrary evidence, publish it.

If a source has been misrepresented, demonstrate how.

If a fact is wrong, show us the correct fact.

That is how serious journalism works.

Not through theatrical declarations.

Not through lengthy moral lectures.

Not through calling another outlet “cowardly.”

WE DO NOT FEAR YOUR CRITICISM

We actually welcome serious criticism.

What we reject is the idea that criticism becomes authoritative simply because it is long.

Your article is lengthy.

But length does not equal depth.

A 5,000-word argument can still be shallow.

A 10,000-word argument can still lack evidence.

A short factual correction can be more powerful than pages of accusations.

Journalism is not measured by word count.

It is measured by facts, evidence, accuracy, relevance, fairness and public interest.

Therefore, if your objective was to educate The Watchdog Media, then perhaps the first lesson is this:

Do not confuse verbosity with authority.

BUILD YOUR CAREER BEFORE YOU TRY TO DISMANTLE OUR CREDIBILITY

We have no interest in destroying your career.

On the contrary, we encourage you to build one.

If Agamlong English Daily Newspaper is genuinely your professional project, rebuild it.

Make it sustainable.

Publish consistently.

Develop a newsroom.

Train journalists.

Investigate stories.

Correct mistakes.

Earn readers.

Build credibility.

Let your work speak.

Then, after establishing a sustained record of professional journalism, you will have an even stronger foundation from which to challenge other media organizations.

But attempting to discredit The Watchdog Media does not automatically make Agamlong English Daily Newspaper more credible.

Our failure, if any, cannot become your success.

And our criticism cannot become your professional résumé.

WE WILL NOT BE INTIMIDATED BY THE WORD “LEGAL”

You also warned that journalists may eventually be required to defend their publications before authorities or courts.

That is understood.

Every responsible media organization recognizes that journalism carries legal responsibilities.

But legal responsibility applies equally to everyone.

If a person believes that a publication is defamatory or false, the appropriate mechanisms exist.

We are not frightened by accountability.

Neither should you be.

If you have a legitimate complaint against a particular publication, identify it and use the appropriate professional or legal mechanisms.

But repeatedly invoking courts, defamation and political consequences in a general attack does not automatically make your argument stronger.

Evidence makes arguments stronger.

SOUTH SUDAN NEEDS MORE JOURNALISTS, NOT MORE SELF-APPOINTED REFEREES

South Sudan needs journalists who investigate.

South Sudan needs journalists who question officials.

South Sudan needs journalists who expose corruption.

South Sudan needs journalists who challenge powerful individuals.

South Sudan needs journalists who ask uncomfortable questions.

But South Sudan also needs journalists who can tolerate criticism themselves.

The media cannot demand transparency from government while refusing transparency internally.

The media cannot demand accountability from politicians while refusing accountability itself.

The media cannot condemn propaganda while publishing political assumptions as established truth.

And journalists cannot demand professional respect without demonstrating professional discipline.

SO, USTAZ SIMON MACHUAR, HERE IS OUR RESPONSE

You asked The Watchdog Media to “bring the evidence.”

We hear you.

Now we ask you to do the same.

Bring the evidence that The Watchdog Media is a political propaganda organization.

Bring the evidence that our stories are deliberately manufactured.

Bring the evidence that we knowingly publish false allegations.

These are legitimate questions.

Economic Reform Committee Advances Security Reforms and Salary Payments

JUBA, South Sudan — The Ministerial High-Level Committee on Economic Reform has stepped up efforts to strengthen security arrangements and accelerate policy implementation across South Sudan following consultations with senior security officials.

Chaired by General Pieng Deng Kuol, the committee briefed security leaders on its recent assessments along key routes, including the Nimule Highway, Jebel Ladu, and Yei Road.

Committee Rapporteur James Mawich said the committee recommended the removal of illegal checkpoints and a reduction in the number of security forces deployed along major roads to improve movement and ease pressure on the public.

On salary payments, the committee said army salaries have been fully paid, while payments for the police and other organized forces are ongoing. Salaries for civil servants are expected to begin within the week.

Singer Deng Mtoto Releases New Song Honoring Benjamin Bol Mel and Aweil Generals

JUBA, South Sudan — South Sudanese singer Deng Mtoto has released a new song titled “Mading Aweil Aweel Rot,” a powerful musical dedication to Dr. Benjamin Bol Mel, former Vice President, and several prominent generals from Aweil.

In the song, Deng Mtoto recognizes a number of Aweil’s senior military figures, including Gen. Malong Awan, Gen. Santino Deng Wol, Gen. Abuk Abuk, Gen. Jiel Mangok, Gen. Akuei Abusala, Gen. Malong Agat, Gen. Agon Ungom Chut, and Gen. Dau Aturjong.

The singer also takes aim at those who question the meaning or truth behind the phrase “Mading Aweil Aweel Rot.” He warns critics against dismissing the message, comparing such an act to “picking a scorpion by its tail.”

Through the song, Deng Mtoto celebrates the influence, achievements, and legacy of prominent personalities from Aweil, turning the track into both a musical tribute and a reflection of the community’s pride in its notable sons.

My Personal Opinion on the Aneet Conflict Between Ngok and Twic

As a concerned citizen, I believe the conflict in Aneet must not continue to claim the lives of our young people from both Twic and Ngok.

Aneet should be a place of security and stability, not a battlefield between communities. In my view, it is supposed to be a military area where only authorized security personnel should be stationed—not a place for competing civilian claims or armed confrontation.

We must have the courage to choose dialogue over violence, coexistence over division, and the future of our young people over the conflicts of the past.

The people of Twic and Ngok are not enemies. They are South Sudanese whose lives, dignity, and future deserve protection. Let us put down the weapons, respect human life, and pursue a peaceful and lasting solution through responsible leadership and dialogue.

Peace is not weakness. Choosing peace is an act of courage and vision.

Voice of patriotic soldier Gen. Mike Mike

South Sudan’s Voter Registration Moving Slowly

The National Election Commission voter registration across South Sudan is moving slowly. Since June 2026, the number of registered voters is still low as one month and half passed.

In the Bahr El Ghazal region, 890,457 people have registered. This is the highest number so far. However, in Equatoria, only 71,908 people have registered. Upper Nile has even fewer, with just 55,723 registered voters.

Election officials are worried about the low numbers in some areas. They are asking all citizens to come forward and register before the deadline. Without enough registered voters, the election results may not fully represent the people.

The Commission is working to speed up the process. They want to make sure every citizen has a chance to take part in the coming elections. Many people have cast doubt on December 22 Voting as security situation continue to deteriorate. 

Watchdog Press reached out to Electoral Commission SG Gabriel Bol Deng who on phone call confirmed the terrible problems facing the Commission that and these problems are likely to affect the 2026 scheduled General Elections.

text:
Breaking News: Massive Revenue Collection at Nimule Border Raises Concerns, as Muon Deng Ajuet Diverted them to his Banks Acount

Juba, South Sudan – We have obtained exclusive figures on the money collected by the South Sudan National Revenue Authority at the Nimule Border during the month of August 2026.

According to the official numbers, the authority collected a total of 40,531,656,846 South Sudanese Pounds and 8,627,627 United States Dollars.

However, our sources within the Revenue Authority have revealed troubling information about how these funds are being handled.

We have learned that the Commissioner General, Hon. Moun Deng Ajuet, has privately instructed that the US dollar amount be deposited into a private company's bank account in Kampala, Uganda. This means the millions in foreign currency will not go into government accounts as expected.

Meanwhile, the entire sum collected in South Sudanese Pounds, over 40 billion SSP, will be packed into sacks and transported to Juba by road this coming Friday.

Our investigative team is following this story closely. The decision to send public money to a private account in another country raises serious questions about transparency and accountability. Many will wonder why revenue meant for the people of South Sudan is being handled in this secretive manner.

We have reached out to the National Revenue Authority and the Commissioner General's office for comments, but they have not yet responded to our requests.

This development comes at a time when South Sudan is struggling with economic challenges, and every money collected at borders is vital for public services and development.

We will continue to monitor this situation and bring you updates as more information becomes available.

Watchdog Press – Watching Your Future

Breaking: Power Stuggle in South Sudan People Defend Forces (SSPDF)

A power struggle is unfolding within South Sudan’s military and political circles. Two officials, Paul Nang and Hussein Abdelbagi, are reportedly working together to remove General Santino Deng Wol from his position as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF).

Their alliance appears to be built on shared ambition rather than political loyalty. Paul Nang, who previously served as CDF and is now an Undersecretary for Veterans Affaird in ministry of Defend,  and a member of the ruling SPLM party, is coordinating with Hussein Abdelbagi, a SOA opposition figure who has regained the Vice Presidency last year. When Hussein was reappointed, Paul Nang quickly went to his home to congratulated him, a move that insiders say was not just courtesy, but a signal of their new partnership.

So why do they want General Santino Deng Wol out? The answer seems to be about the future succession. Behind closed doors, they are reportedly using the President’s poor health as a justification for their plans. They are telling allies that if the President becomes incapacitated, they, not the military under Deng Wol, should take over. In their vision, General Deng Wol is a major obstacle. As a respected and legitimate military leader, he stands in the way of their political ambitions. Removing him would clear the path for their takeover and that is why they doing black and white to remove him.

To achieve this, both men are said to be offering bribes and making secret deals to win support from other officials who are influencial around President Kiir. Their goal is to weaken the chain of command and replace it with their own arrangement. However, their strategy is risky. By bypassing proper procedures and conspiring across party lines, they are testing the limits of the country’s fragile peace.

For now, General Santino remains in his post. But the political atmosphere is tense. If these people truly succeed, everyone must know what is at stake is not just one man’s job, but the stability of the entire military, and possibly the nation itself.

text:
The Misadventures of Larson Angok Garang Weu South Sudan’s Most Hungry Commercial Musician

Once upon a time in South Sudan, there lived a man named Larson Angok. Larson is not your average musician, he is a commercial artist whose music can't pay lunch. His songs are so forgettable that even his mother hums them wrong when singing in Korok Achien Yor vilage. So, instead of writing good tunes, Larson invented a new hobby: fighting with everyone who has more money than him to be bribed with handouts.

First, he fought poor Tut Kew until Tut gave him a car and some cash just to shut up. Larson sold the car, spent the money on roasted Nyama-Choma and merisa (local brew) in Abyei Chok, and when his pocket was empty again, he looked for his next meal ticket. He started screaming at a woman named Achai Wiir Awet Alor, threatening to release a diss track with tittled "Baal Ariik Panther." Achai, who does not play games, seriously promised to castrate Larson with her own hands and turned him into a soprano if that song ever drops. To this day, we are still waiting. The song is as coming-soon as rain in February.

But Larson’s real jealousy is legendary. When young Abraham Welldone showed up in music some years back, with better vocals, Larson didn't compete peacefully, he work hard to make sure that he helped young artist into an early grave just to claim the copyrights of his songs. Yes, he stole a dead man’s playlist and as of now, he proudly singing the songs "I backward from Ghana" and "Ke toc wai," a  classy lyrics he inherited from Abraham Weldone after he killed him.

After finishing burrying Weldone in a shallow grave in Mading Aweil, Larson, then set his jealous eyes on Dau Mobatel, because Dau’s voice sounds a tiny bit like his and more vocal than him. Larson visited every witch-doctor from Equatoria to Awan-yien and Guang-nou in Bahr el Ghazal. And from across the region, paying every witch-doctor with promises and empty soda bottles, to put a curse on Dau but failed. When magic failed, Angok tried to sell Dau out to criminals. But Dau is no fool, he wears his protection like a second skin and has more charm than a snake charmer. Dau saw Larson’s plots from a mile away and laughed so hard he nearly choked on his kisra.

Defeated and desperate, Larson ran to the studio and recorded angry songs about Dau. But in every verse, he accidentally insulted himself so badly that even his own microphone felt embarrassed. The songs backfired harder than a rusty tuk-tuk (rickshaw). Dau rsponded with meaningful diss songs of "Manh achep-chep" a song that shaken Angok's mother grinding stone in Korok Achien Yor. Desperate and confused, Angok accused John Kudusay of composing the dissing songs for Dau mobatel and started fighting every Artist in Aweil east. That is the beginning Angok's downfall in the music till date. you can not combine the ego and jealousy and expect success.

Now, broke and out of enemies, Larson is clinging to the leg of a kind businesswoman, and pillanthropist, Ayen Ngong, hoping she will give him "handouts." But Ayen is not a fool she is sharpening her pangaa (machete) of life lessons. Larson is currently on the run, hiding behind a mango tree around Juba, and sweating more than a politician in a corruption hearing.

The police are looking for him and he hide himself like Tom who has seen Jere in Tom and Jere movie. The courts are waiting. And soon, Larson Angok will have to answer for his crimes: jealousy, bad music, and wasting everyone's time. In South Sudan, we say, "A hungry dog chases many bones." But this dog has just bit himself.

The Mobilization of Nuer Fighters by Abur Chol and Kuol Kuol Dau Raises Fears of Family Cleansing in Tonj North While the Online Governor Bol Wek Is Sleeping in Juba

JUBA, South Sudan — An organized mobilization of armed Nuer fighters to target members of the Paan Ariik and Apukpadoc communities has raised fears of further bloodshed, family cleansing, and displacement following deadly attacks and cattle raids in Tonj North, Warrap State.

Abur Chol, described by community sources as a controversial and blood-thirsty Lou Mawien Ariik community leader in Juba, and the quack businessman Kuol Kuol Dau are mobilizing Nuer fighters from Bul Nuer in Mayom County to attack members of the Paan Ariik and Apukpadoc communities.

The allegations come amid claims that armed youths are being mobilized not only to target communities in rural areas but also Paan Ariik residents living in major towns, including Juba, Wau, and Warrap.

Speaking about the conflict, Abur Chol was quoted as saying:

“When I fell out with Moulana Kuol Makol Ariik in Khartoum, I swore to him that I would destroy Lou Ariik and that all shall come begging me on their knees. And indeed, as of today, the mission is 90% accomplished.”

The statement, according to people familiar with the gathering, was delivered confidently and received applause from the attendees.

Businessman Kuol Kuol Dau was also quoted as describing his willingness to commit substantial financial resources to the conflict and mobilize fighters against Paan Ariik communities.

“I have never been so much into this conflict as I have been recently. I have to fight this war even if it means spending millions of dollars. I have enough cash to mobilize Nuer mercenaries to deal with Paan Ariik in Apuk and Looth youth in towns to deal with Paan Ariik, especially in Juba, Wau, Warrap, and even in Kenya and Uganda.”

Kuol Kuol Dau is described as a fake businessman who connives with senior government officials to win unproductive road construction contracts.

The remarks, if authentic and accurately contextualized, would indicate an intention to extend the conflict beyond cattle camps and into urban communities where civilians from the affected groups reside.

Earlier Confrontation

The latest allegations follow an earlier confrontation in 2025 when, according to community sources, armed Nuer fighters were brought in during an attempted cattle raid at Achongchong Cattle Camp.

The Paan Ariik resisted the raid and recovered their cattle. However, community sources said the confrontation resulted in more than 10 deaths and left 26 people wounded.

On August 9, 2026, the same sources stated that Nuer fighters were again mobilized and attacked Paan Ariik and Apukpadoc cattle camps at Athieng in Akop Payam.

According to the accounts, more than 60 people were killed and more than 10,000 cattle were looted in the attack.

The reported death toll and number of cattle taken could not be independently verified.

Akook Boma Attack

In what sources described as a simultaneous attack, armed Looth youths ruthlessly attacked Akook Boma, where they killed elderly residents, looted property, and set over 500 houses ablaze.

The attacks forced thousands of civilians—including women, children, and elderly people—to flee their homes.

The violence has heightened concerns that the conflict could spread from cattle camps and rural areas to towns and other locations where members of the communities live.

Community sources further state that Abur Chol and Kuol Kuol Dau are among the key mobilizers and financiers of the conflict, while Maj. Gen. Kuol Akoon Mathoor and Brig. Gen. Kook Bierkuei Mawien, both officers in the South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF), are accused of supplying assorted arms and ammunition to the Nuer fighters. The sources further claim that the two officers have access to military arms and ammunition storage facilities at Bilpam, a claim that could not be independently verified at the time of publication.

Community sources are calling for authorities to investigate the attacks, establish responsibility for the killings and property losses, and take measures to prevent further attacks against civilians.

Regional News: UPDF, RDF Reaffirm Commitment to Stronger Military Cooperation

Reported by Kamukama

The Uganda Peoples’ Defence Forces (UPDF) 2 Infantry Division and Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) 5 Infantry Division have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening military cooperation, building trust and promoting peace and stability along the Uganda-Rwanda border.

The commitment was made during the Eighth Proximity Commanders’ Meeting held in Mbarara City.

Major General Felix Busizori, Deputy Commander of Land Forces, commended the leadership of President Yoweri Museveni of Uganda and President Paul Kagame of Rwanda for supporting continued engagement between the two forces.

Major General Paul Muhanguzi, Commander of the UPDF 2 Infantry Division, emphasised the importance of maintaining strong relations with border communities, describing them as a critical source of security information.

Speaking for the RDF delegation, Brigadier General Ruki Karusisi commended the UPDF leadership for its commitment to strengthening relations between the two armies.

The engagement also featured a joint Civil-Military Cooperation (CIMIC) activity in Kamwezi, where UPDF and RDF personnel planted more than 80 trees.

The commanders reaffirmed that continued cooperation, trust and open dialogue remain vital to peace, security and economic development along the Uganda-Rwanda border.

A Resolution of Maturity, Humanity and National Unity: Watchdog Press Withdraws Athieng Riiny Thiik from Its List of Engagements

This is an official update on our recent post about a beautiful girl – Athieng Riiny Thiik

Good evening, young lady, Athieng Riiny Thiik,

First and foremost, we believe that disagreements and conflicts should never take away our humanity, mutual respect, unity or commitment to peace. While we remain firm in pursuing truth and holding accountable those we believe stand against our agenda, we also recognize the importance of maturity, reconciliation, and peaceful engagement.

This statement is therefore intended to officially communicate to you that the previously prepared heavy missiles against you has been withdrawn. Our assigned committee comprising two male and one female professional writers from different backgrounds has been directed by the Watchdog Press Management to remove your name from the list of individuals previously identified for further engagement, including Larson Angok Garang Weu, Becky Akuindik Abiem, and others who are evidently discovered as part of those standing on the way of agenda.

With immediate effect, you are free from any further retaliatory engagement from our platform. We will continue to focus on issues and individuals that we believe are directly connected to political activities against our agenda. You may therefore rest assured that you will not see or hear further negative publications about yourself from our page.

This decision takes effect today, Sunday, 30th August 2026, and is unconditional.

Our decision comes out of respect for a genuine appeal made by a highly respected gentleman, as well as your humble and mature reaction to our recent post that featured your latest photographs. Your response demonstrated maturity and reflected the principles of humanity, dignity, and peaceful coexistence.

We expected a harsh and aggressive reaction from you and those who support you. However, you and others responded in a manner completely different from what we anticipated. Some members of our team even expected the situation to escalate, but you proved them wrong through your restraint and maturity.

For that, we sincerely thank you.

Your response has challenged us to see you as someone who genuinely values peace, mutual respect, unity, and coexistence among our people. We have taken note of that, and we respect it.

We also extend our sincere appreciation to the respected gentleman who, despite the demands of his busy schedule in Juba, took the time to reach out to us through a third party. We regard him as a true nationalist and a youthful leader who deserves respect and support whenever necessary. His intervention, combined with your mature response, greatly contributed to this decision.

As citizens and members of one nation, we must always remember that disagreements should not permanently divide us. South Sudan needs young people who can rise above insults, hostility, and personal differences in order to promote peace, unity, and national understanding.

Should you wish to know the identity of the gentleman whose name has been withheld, you are welcome to contact us through Messenger by call or text message.

Our best wishes are with you. We will continue to pray that God blesses your future, grants you happiness, and, according to His will, blesses you with a responsible and loving husband who will stand by you throughout your life.

“If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.” — Romans 12:18

How Gen. Akot Abiem is planning to reignit Apuk-Aguok communal conflict? A dangerous plan to restart the old conflict between the Apuk and Aguok Kuei communities in Gogrial of Warrap State has been uncovered. This comes just as the two communities were finally enjoying the peace they signed back at around 2016-2017. After years of fighting, the people were beginning to trust each other again and they are now living peacefully. But recently, one man is trying to burn it all down for his own selfish gain.

That man is Brigadier General Akot Abiem Akeen of the Aguok Kuei community. According to our sources, Akot recently called a secret meeting at his home in Thongpiny. He gathered only his close relatives and some community elders whom he thought could listen to his idea. But this was not a meeting to discuss development or unity. text:
When Black Gold Becomes Black Poison

By Johnbasco Adhar

Passing the Cybersecurity Law in the Republic of South Sudan will not scare the many young South Sudanese who have chosen truth over favouritism and continue debating issues facing society and speaking the truth, despite the high level of intimidation.

Her Excellency Mama Rebecca Nyandeng De Mabior recently delivered a speech to a congregation in Juba. The words and truths she spoke once again shook the entire nation and many people and were widely shared by social media users and netizens across the world..

There is also the controversial debate surrounding the prophecy of a man who claims to be a prophet. It is not difficult for God to convey His messages to South Sudanese because, after twenty-one years of oppression, God can grant freedom.

In these two important moments, Mama Rebecca and Pastor Peter have spoken. However, beyond their speeches and the ongoing debates, my own analysis is simple:

The oil is cursed, and black gold has become black poison.

How can oil and gold beneath the ground become cursed?

South Sudan's oil has often been described as a blessing, yet its story has largely been one of deep destruction.

Beyond the billions allegedly stolen, oil has shaped the nation's politics, fuelled war, created dependency, destroyed communities, and silenced citizens.

Oil wealth has instead brought frustration and sadness to many South Sudanese.

A few individuals within the government have used oil money to create divisions and fuel communal conflicts rather than promote development.

The 2013–2018 civil war was financed largely by oil revenues. Both government and armed factions used oil income to pay their forces, buy weapons, and maintain control over oil-producing regions.

Meanwhile, the environmental toll of oil extraction has been immense. Oil spills from ageing pipelines, toxic waste, and the dumping of contaminated water have caused serious damage.

As a result, Bentiu, Akobo, and Panriang remain among the major productive oil areas with little development.

People living near oil operation fields have become victims of illness, lost farmland, and displacement without compensation.

International contractors, especially those from China, have largely remained silent without enforcing adequate safety regulations.

With an economy entirely dependent on a single commodity, the nation was engineered to fail.

Oil's presence made disputes economically valuable, while tribal identity made them emotionally charged.

If oil had been managed transparently and equitably, South Sudan could have built a sovereign wealth fund to save revenue for future generations, provide a financial cushion against price shocks, invest in education, and modernise healthcare systems to reduce maternal mortality and treat preventable diseases.

Roads, electricity, and clean drinking water could have reached every community, while the economy could have been diversified through agriculture.

Industries, manufacturing factories, and service sectors could have reduced dependency on oil and created jobs.

Instead, national oil resources have been turned into instruments of personal interest, fuelled conflict, and confused the youth.

Oil itself is not cursed.

It is leaders who have governed the nation through corruption, tribalism, and self-interest who have turned a national blessing into poison.

Development funds became personal wealth, communities became war zones, and the potential story of prosperity became a tragedy.

The oil remains in the ground, and the wealth still exists. With wise leaders, South Sudan can still have a bright future ahead.

But without leaders committed to serving the nation rather than themselves, that potential will continue to be squandered, and oil will remain more of a curse than a promise.

God has heard the grievances of the people of South Sudan and will answer their prayers very soon, not later.

The author is an aspiring journalist Johnbasco Adhar

Storytelling Compared with the Leadership of Our Liberators Who Are in Charge

By Cde Bil Riar

During the rainy season, Sultan Awan Muorkuau, the fox, visited his sister’s husband, Mr. Maloudit, the elephant.

The elephant had already called the whole village to cultivate. Everyone was working hard.

His wife asked, “Why call so many people when we don’t even have enough oil for cooking?”

The elephant calmly said, “Don’t worry. Just cook. I will handle it.”

Sultan watched carefully and whispered, “Ah… this is powerful leadership.”

After farming, the food was ready. The elephant did something confident and strange near the cooking area—and somehow everything worked. Everyone ate happily.

Sultan’s eyes widened. “I understand everything now!”

He rushed home and said, “Invite everyone tomorrow! I will handle everything like my brother-in-law!”

His wife was shocked. “But we don’t have enough oil!”

Sultan said proudly, “Just cook!”

The next day, after cultivation, the food was ready. Sultan tried to copy the elephant’s “method,” but he misunderstood everything and ended up jumping away, shouting, “Leadership is burning me!”

When Mr. Maloudit arrived, he laughed and said:

“My brother-in-law, you copied the action but not the leadership.”

So, can somebody pass this storytelling to Mr. PhD Thai-Thai at J1 and President Salva Kiir Kuethpiny Mayardit, that you are stuck and have copied family leadership, which has left you stuck even in the leadership of the animal that represents you, since your identity exists?

It would be good if President Kiir copied the leadership of William Deng Nhial or his comrade, Dr. John Garang, instead of creating genocide among the 64 tribes while pretending that he has done nothing. He is the first president of the Republic of South Sudan.

Don’t copy what you see—understand it first.

Cde Bil Riar
Son of Tonjdit Kalkuel

OFFICIAL PUBLIC STATEMENT ON PEACE, UNITY AND DEVELOPMENT IN WARRAP STATE

BY CDE BIL RIAR 
SON OF TONJDIT KALKUEL 

WARRAP PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVE (WPDI)

The Warrap Peace and Development Initiative (WPDI) recognizes that the recurring violence affecting Warrap State, particularly in Greater Tonj, constitutes not merely a security challenge, but a profound obstacle to social cohesion, governance and sustainable development.

WPDI therefore calls for a new political and civic commitment to peace—one founded upon dialogue, responsible leadership, rule of law, reconciliation and inclusive development.

We firmly reject revenge violence, collective punishment, hate speech and the normalization of communal conflict. No grievance should be allowed to justify the loss of innocent lives or the destruction of communities.

WPDI calls upon the Government of Warrap State, traditional authorities, political leaders, intellectuals, women, youth, religious institutions and development partners to strengthen permanent mechanisms for mediation, early conflict prevention, accountability and reconciliation.

Greater Tonj requires sustained peacebuilding rather than temporary interventions. Peace agreements must be translated into measurable action, community trust and lasting institutional arrangements. Recent peace dialogues have demonstrated that communities are prepared to pursue reconciliation; the responsibility now is to ensure that commitments are implemented.

We further believe that peace and development are inseparable. Education, employment, agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare and youth empowerment must form part of the state's long-term peace strategy. Current development initiatives in Greater Tonj demonstrate the value of combining livelihood opportunities with peacebuilding and community resilience.

WPDI'S PRINCIPLE IS SIMPLE:
Peace must precede prosperity, justice must accompany reconciliation, and development must reach every community.

We call upon the people of Warrap to reject the inheritance of violence and embrace a new political culture founded upon unity, dignity, responsible citizenship and peaceful coexistence.
Warrap must not be defined by its conflicts.
Warrap must be defined by the future it chooses to build.

Warrap Peace and Development Initiative (WPDI)
For Peace. For Unity. For Justice. For Sustainable Development.
One Warrap. One Future. One Peace.

topComments.text: This statement "I am sick but I came because my doctors are here" may also mean, the president has been sicked of National issues in his Country and had to traveled to South Africa to seek some solutions/advices to help him resolve the numerous problems in South Sudan.

text:
Press Secretary to the President Salva Kiir, Arek Aldo Ajou Deng Akuei, is too harsh on the Vice President Rebecca Nyandeng De Mabior, the wife of the founding father.

That is why liberators deserve to speak for themselves not the opportunists who never contributed in the revolution and in regards to their differences and existing historical rhetorics. Dr. Aldo Ajou himself is a seasonal critic to President Salva Kiir- that goes without denial despite being in exile during the liberation struggle. 

Aldo Ajou daughter who grew up in the UK became the mouth piece for President on connections and the fragility of the Presidency, now terribly vilifying those who had suffered together with SKM in the war while her family was enjoying and watching the struggle on international channels and radios.

Even the General elections Arek is advocating loudly, hasn't secured the 250 millions budgeted for its conduct- Professor Abenego Akok Kachuol, chairman of electoral commission acknowledged the impossibility of the process in his recent Eye Radio interview. 

Anyone in his/her rational mind can measure the time against the preparation of the electoral process and it parameters. There is going to be no elections and if at all, there is going to be elections in December this year, it would be a shame the country wouldn't recover from, like any other disgrace  of mismanagement of resources  and dysfunctional administration seen in years. 

Rebecca Nyandeng de Mabior doesn't deserve to be critize  by the calibers of Aldo Ajou or his siblings. May be the siblings of the revolutionaries who immensely contributed during the the years of inevitable struggle that culminated to what we now all claimed today as solemn contribution of everyone.

A spokesperson to the President should be one that looked at the bigger picture, rather than the one engrossed in the decisive politics and national disintegration. Dr John Garang's family is too heavy to be critize by the Londoners, it might consequentially backfire even with elections being falsely emphasized. That is why John Garang's portrait lies in the center of our national currencies with no opposition from the diversities of the national set up. Try SKM portrait for currencies and face an unending debate for qualification.

My take on the hihly publicized and non-funded elections is ready and was delayed due to the recent double loss of my uncles and community members who died a week after another! 

The country is at crossroads, therefore, hate speech and English coherency shouldn't be used unnecessarily. To paraphrase, President Kiir is not eloquent in speaking English language but he had served the nation as President for two decades. 

Arek's queen english with limited liberation history shoud not become the sharpened tool to destroy what she and the entire family never built during the liberation struggle and in the interim period-alike! Thank you anyway Madam PS for revealing to the entire nation that the President is suffering from dementia- a credit for your conversation time with your loved ones as Press Secretary to the President!

By 1610354657:2048:Emmanuel Ariech Deng Part 3

text:
Another Video of Shame by the Queen of Incompetency Who Is Betraying South Sudan Sovereignty Abroad

The media, led by the brain-handicapped Arek Aldo, should allow such videos showing handshakes between two presidents, but not conversations.

The brain-handicapped Press Secretary, Arek Aldo Ajou, the most incompetent press secretary in the history of South Sudan, has messed up again.

Arek selects untrained journalists for lucrative trips to South Sudan, leaving out well-trained and professional journalists. In Juba, such incompetence is a total disgrace to our country.

Watchdog Press – Watching Your Future

URGENT PUBLIC AWARENESS — REPORTED ATTACK IN TONJ NORTH COUNTY

By our correspondent on the ground 

According to reports, Pan Ariik-Longar Agok Kuch, with mobilized armed youths from both Apuk Padoc Community and Nuer militias, carried out a coordinated serious armed attack at approximately 5:15 a.m. on Thursday, 27 August 2026, at Machar Pakuek cattle camps in the Konggor area and Alabek Payam, Tonj North County.

According to these reports, more than 70 people were reportedly killed, and about 50 others were injured. Thousands of cattle were also reportedly raided, with some of the cattle later recovered by Lou Mawien Ariik Community youths.

Local authorities reportedly indicate that this incident is part of a repeated pattern of attacks in the area by the same criminals.

We call on the national and state governments, security authorities, humanitarian organizations, and independent investigators to urgently establish the facts, protect civilians, provide medical assistance to the injured, and ensure accountability for those responsible.

The reported loss of life is deeply concerning. Civilians must not become victims of violence, and communities should avoid retaliation or collective blame while the facts are being established.

We urge the authorities to provide the public with a transparent and timely account of what happened at Machar Pakuek and to take immediate measures to prevent further violence.

Our thoughts are with the victims, the injured, and their families.
