text:
NILEPET's Managing Director, Emmanuel Athiei, organized a dinner yesterday at the Pyramid Intercontinental Hotel, where members of his close circle within Nilepet, as well as political allies and their families, were invited.

Sources claimed that an inflated bill of more than US$500,000 was paid. They also claimed that a single dish cost US$200. When pocket money for attendees was added, the total expenditure was said to have reached US$1 million.

These figures have not been independently verified. However, the dinner itself is confirmed to have taken place.

topComments.text:
You guys are exaggerating. A buffet typically costs around US$30–35 per person, including drinks. The hall accommodates a maximum of about 230 people. Even at US$35 per person, that’s approximately US$8,050 for catering. Adding an estimated US$3,000 for the hall and other event expenses, the total cost would still likely be well under US$15,000.

Before publishing figures as high as US$500,000 or US$1 million, there should be credible evidence. Spreading unverified numbers only misleads the public.

Deng Dut Koor’s Mother Appeals to President Salva Kiir for Mercy

The mother of government critic Deng Dut Koor has made a heartfelt public appeal to President Salva Kiir Mayardit, asking him to forgive her son and grant him mercy.

Deng Dut Koor was arrested in February. In her appeal, his mother pleaded with the President to show compassion and pardon her son, expressing hope for his release.

📸: Nyan Maguangdit

Deng Dut Koor’s Mother Pleads with President Kiir for Mercy

The mother of government critic Deng Dut Koor has publicly appealed to President Salva Kiir Mayardit to forgive her son and show him mercy.

Deng Dut Koor was arrested in Nairobi in February before being transferred to South Sudan.

text:
Leak of A Mounting Pressure on NILEPET's MD Emmanuel Athiei Ayual as Calls for Leadership Change Intensifies 

NILEPET Managing Director Emmanuel Athiei appears to be under mounting pressure amid growing speculation that his tenure could come to an end. Sources familiar with the matter say MD Athiei previously expressed confidence that his position was secure, arguing that it formed part of an arrangement linked to the family of Anok Salva and suggesting that key Government positions had been shared among members of President Salva Kiir's family.

According to sources, concerns over his possible dismissal prompted Athiei to bring foreign partners to meet President Kiir and present information indicating that South Sudan's oil production had surpassed 100,000 barrels per day. Observers note that similar production figures were announced by former Petroleum Undersecretary Dr. Chol Deng shortly before he was removed from office.

Sources also indicate that President Kiir is facing increasing pressure from officials in Warrap State, who have criticized Athiei's management of NILEPET and are urging that new leadership be appointed.

One outspoken elder argued that if the position is intended for Anok Salva Kiir's family, then it should be filled by a more capable and competent individual, insisting that Athiei should be replaced.

Conclusion

With concerns over leadership, management, and confidence in NILEPET continuing to surface, many stakeholders believe the company would benefit from new leadership. They argue that appointing a competent and experienced Managing Director would strengthen governance, improve accountability, and restore confidence in the national oil company. As a result, they recommend that President Kiir remove Emmanuel Athiei and appoint a qualified successor to lead NILEPET forward.

We don't have selfish interests attached to this call but we are just speaking truth in favor of countless voiceless citizens.

text:
Leak of Power Struggle Within SPLM and Growing Political Influence

A severe power struggle is looming within the ruling SPLM, with leak reports indicating that the party's Secretary-General, Dr. Akol Paul Kordit, has positioned himself as a co-president. A situation not far away from what grounded former VP Dr. Benjamin Bol Mel.

Reliable sources that are working in certain institutions of the Juba Regime strongly that SG Dr. Akol Paul has been orchestrating political maneuvers to shield his close allies accused of corruption, including NILEPET's Managing Director Emmanuel Athiei Ayual. In his tactics of political protecting Athiei, he always claims that MD Athiei is doing everything in the best interests of the top leadership therefore he must be given a long time to achieve more.

According to the sources, one of these tactics and strategies is to portray these officials as indispensable to the government so that, if they are removed, the President would appear to be dismissing competent public servants. Key members within the ruling party and security sector further argued that Dr. Akol Paul is the primary beneficiary of his association with these officials.

As an example, the sources stressed out that the tarmacking project carried out last week within the NILEPET's premises cost approximately $2 million and was awarded to a company linked to Dr. Akol Paul Koordit. This is an open corruption scandal committed by one of the top Government officials who is supposed to discourage the practice of corruption.

The sources also said that DPOC deposited $13 million into a NILEPET account yesterday and that the funds are being shared among political allies.

According to these leak reports (various sources), it is clear of no question that Dr. Akol Paul is attempting to pressure the President by publicly praising officials who have faced corruption accusations, with the aim of influencing Presidential decisions and making any action taken without his approval appear politically damaging.

Watchdog Press – Watching Your Future

TONJ SOUTH MASTERCLASS IN PEACEKEEPING (2016–2026)
The Village Champion: Isaac Ismael Akech Tong

Incident 1 – 2016

In 2016, Akech Tong sent an army tanker to Thony Community after an incident in Wunkech. Civilians from Thony Community were killed in cold blood, including one woman. After this incident, he completely distanced himself from Tonj South and moved to the state level. This was driven by his hatred toward Thony Community because it is the hometown of Nhial Deng Nhial, with whom he had differences. He was trying to provoke Nhial and Wol Mayom Bol, as he saw Wol as a threat to his ministerial ambitions. The attack killed several young men from Thony Community, including Akuma Ater Nai and Kuluel Jang. They were shot at the Wunkech cattle camp.

Incident 2 – 20 May 2026

On 20 May 2026, Akech Tong, through security officers in WarGiir, coordinated an attack on Thony Community. Youths from neighboring communities such as Yar, Muok, and Apuk Juwiir were involved. The attack was later stopped when Ding Ding Tong from Muok Community warned the others that Thony Community had been alerted and advised them to attack in the morning instead.

During that clash, eleven lives were lost in the Amethchok/Makuei Kerthith incident. A total of 118 cows raided from Thony Community were taken to Akech Tong's compound in WarGiir and divided, with Akech Tong receiving a share from the youths of Muok.

If Ismael Isaac and the county government were committed to peace, they would not have allowed this incident to happen. Since Amethchok is part of Tonj Town and is only a 10-minute drive away, this clearly shows how Thony has been targeted by these politicians by being drawn into conflict with its sister communities. It is also true that Tonj South has never been at peace since the day Ismael Isaac stepped foot in Tonj.

Incident 3 – 2024 to 2026

When Muok Community youths could not defeat Thony Community in open battle, they turned to road ambushes. From 2024 to 2026, 103 people were killed in this way, including government officials from Thony Community.

Tonj South was described as peaceful before Akech Tong, also known as Ismael Isaac, arrived. It is no wonder that the respected local chief, Malok Akot Wut, later disowned him, saying he had come to understand that Akech's motives were to destroy the people of Tonj South.

Incident 4 – 14 June 2026

On 14 June 2026, Akech Tong made an unofficial visit to his home village. A meeting there was followed by surprise attacks on Sunday evening against Thony Community in Pinybarkou.

He spent two days in WarGiir Boma before leaving Tonj at night and arriving in Juba at around 5:30 p.m. He left behind four boxes of AKM ammunition, four PKM machine guns, and 70 new black AK-47 rifles. He also secured the release of detained elders from Muok so they could mobilize to "end Thony Community completely."

Most Recent

Following a voice note from John Garang Mabior Ater, Akech Tong and his allies pressured the commissioner's office to release a statement claiming that police had been sent to disperse the warring communities. However, Pinybarkou is a village in Thony, raising the question of how civilians could have been shot in their own homes.

Thony Community has suffered greatly. Other communities involved have witnessed the violence but do not admit the truth. The conflict in Tonj South is being fueled by Akech Tong, and because he has gone unpunished, he continues to repeat the same actions. Thony Community is ready to meet Akech Tong in court or on the battlefield. We knew he was our leader, but we cannot continue to cover up his actions. Enough is enough.

The Leak: the Juba Regime Opted to Use NSS DG Akech Tong Aleu in Funding Violence Being Used as a Tool for Control in Tonj South County to Pave Ways for Agugo Mining Project 

Residents and community observers in Tonj South County, Warrap State, have raised grave concerns, linking the recent brutality in Thony Community to a wider pattern of manufactured insecurity.

According to these reliable sources, DG Akech Tong Aleu and Wol Amou are being named by locals as being behind the attack on Thony Community. The information suggests that the attack was not random. Instead, critics argue that it fits a deliberate strategy: fuel chaos first, then demand a "solution" that benefits those who created the problem.

The logic goes like this:

1. Escalate insecurity: By sponsoring or enabling violence against civilians in Thony Subsection of Tonj Community, the area is pushed into panic. Fear spreads, markets closed, and people forced to flee.

2. Create demand for troops: As the situation deteriorates, calls grow louder for the government to deploy more security forces to Tonj South County to "restore order."

3. Repurpose the deployment: Once government troops are on the ground, the information is that those same forces are then diverted from civilian protection. Instead, they are used to provide maximum security for private economic interests—specifically, illegal gold mining operations in the Agugo area of Tonj South.

In short, the claim is that human lives are being used as bait. Community suffering becomes the justification for bringing in armed men, and those armed men are then deliberately turned into guards for mining sites rather than protectors of the people.

Why is this being called out so strongly?

People with accurate information point to three things:

1. The timing: Attacks spike right before discussions about deploying new forces or opening up new mining sites.

2. The geography: The violence is centered near routes and areas leading toward Agugo, not necessarily in places with the highest levels of inter-communal tension.

3. The outcome: If troops are deployed but civilians in Thony still do not feel safe while mining sites are heavily guarded, then trust in the government collapses. It appears that the state is protecting gold, not people.

For families in Tonj South, this means they are caught in the middle. They are grieving relatives, losing livestock, and watching children drop out of school while also hearing that their pain is being used to create space for illegal extraction.

The Bigger Picture

Warrap State has experienced cycles of communal violence for years, often tied to cattle, land, and the weak rule of law. When illegal mining enters that mix, critics warn that it adds a profit motive to the violence. It turns insecurity from a problem to be solved into a resource to be managed.

If these claims are true, they would represent a betrayal of public trust by using state security as a private militia. It remains to be seen whether the government will turn a blind eye, especially since it has previously been alleged that the government itself is sponsoring mining, as DG Akech reportedly disclosed.

What's Needed Now

An independent investigation, protection for civilians in Thony, transparent deployment orders for any troops sent to Tonj South, and oversight of mining activities in Agugo are needed to ensure that security forces remain accountable to the public, not to private interests.

Leak from Blue House Leadership through meeting between DG Akech Tong Aleu and some people from his home village 

According to a leaked report, governors and chief administrators were summoned to Juba to meet with the President to discuss two major issues: the upcoming elections and the recruitment of forces from all states and the three Administrative Areas. General Akech explained that the recruitment of new forces will be carried out in the name of the elections, stating that these forces are needed only for election purposes. However, all of the new recruits will be integrated into the NSS Special Forces and the Presidential Special Forces under the Tiger Division as an alternative to the struggling SSPDF.

In a professional analysis of General Akech Tong's comments, the interpretation is that the recruitment is sugar-coated and being presented as part of election preparations, while many believe the real reason is different. According to General Akech Tong, the government does not have enough forces at its disposal, and the recruitment effort is intended to fill that gap.

At the same time, General Akech Tong has reportedly instructed some officers from his home area to privately advise young men to remain focused on agriculture and other life-sustaining activities rather than joining the army to defend what he described as a government already burdened with unmanageable problems. This message suggests that priorities should not be limited to military recruitment but should instead include productive work that can improve livelihoods and strengthen communities.

He also instructed the officers to make it known that he holds a different opinion on the matter so that no one feels left behind in hearing the message he intends civilians to receive.

This position appears to distance him from the official line and suggests that there may be disagreement within the system about the direction being taken. Such differences, if not handled carefully, can create confusion among the public and among the forces themselves.

At a time when the country is facing political uncertainty and growing concerns about security, these developments raise serious questions. If recruitment is being driven by political necessity rather than genuine national security planning, then the public deserves clarity.

Young people should not be misled by promises that do not reflect the real situation on the ground. Instead, they should be encouraged to invest in farming, skills development, and other productive activities that can support both their families and the nation, he said.

This is why the issue should be discussed openly and honestly. People need to know whether the recruitment is truly about elections, security, or simply filling an existing gap in the system. Without clear communication, mistrust will continue to grow.

He completed the NILEPET headquarters after years of delay. The Sham Election Trap and waste of Resources if conducted in December 22nd 2026: South Sudan’s Groups of Leaders and Business People Choose Power and Wealth Over Peace

The current debate about South Sudan’s upcoming election is not a debate about democracy. It is a dangerous charade. Those in power who speak loudly about polling day are not sincere patriots. They are not driven by a vision for peace or a better future for their people and history of sovereignty millions of South Sudanese fought for it in consecutive 21 years of civil war where 2.5 millions people lives were lost. Their only concern is the same old pursuit: retaining wealth and power at any cost even loosing extra lives of over 2.5 millions people.

Let us be clear about what a real democratic path looks like. An election that builds a better foundation for South Sudan's 64 tribes cannot be a quick, exclusionary event. It cannot be a quick mission of individuals whose campaigns and pledges are driven by their personal gains. The election which South Sudanese deserved must be inclusive. This means bringing all political actors to the table, including those who are not currently in the country and those hidden in several dangerous jails in Juba and other places across South Sudan. In other words, this includes holdout groups, civil society representatives, and even armed opposition forces that are fighting the current government. Leaving them out is not democracy or pursuit of genuine peace; it is a recipe for continued war and tactical succession plans.

Furthermore, an election is not a single day activity as some people are claiming. It is the culmination of a long process of preparation to ensure full protection for history and preserve rights of all their voters and those seeking votes as well. Before any credible vote can take place, the entire nation must complete the essential prerequisites. South Sudanese need a permanent constitution that all parties agree upon, to replace the temporary documents that have governed us for too long. As an independent nation, we need a national census to know who we are and where we are. And most critically, we need comprehensive security sector reforms to ensure that the guns are silent and the state’s security forces are neutral protectors of the people, not political weapons prepared to be used against the unwanted opposition parties that have ability to professionally challenge the ruling party. Only after these steps can we hope and talk for a peaceful and credible election.

The unfortunate reality is that the current government has no interest in this inclusive, well-prepared path. They are terrified of a free and fair contest. Why? Because they are the worst-performing officials in South Sudan’s troubled history that we all know. Their tenure has been marked by economic collapse, widespread suffering, and a constant bleed of conflict. They know that if they allow a genuine election, they will be voted out of office by a population that has endured too much pain under their unpatriotic decisions and actions.

Therefore, their plan is simple and cynical: they want to conduct a sham election. A rigged process that will rubber-stamp their continued grip on power and accumulation of wealth. They hope that by putting on a show of voting, they can fool the international community while they continue to plunder the nation's resources. They are willing to let the country bleed further, as long as they remain in their positions of privilege.

This is why some clique running the current government must listen to the wise counsel of the international community and regional bodies like IGAD and AU. The only logical and responsible path forward is to adjourn this election. The already suffering communities need to step back from the brink. The government should stop its posturing and genuinely engage all political actors in a sincere dialogue, not the impose selective peace talks. This is not a sign of weakness; it is the only way to find a better pathway to free, fair, and credible elections that will reflect on the long history of South Sudanese. The choice is stark: pursue a sham vote and deepen the crisis, or postpone and do the hard work of building a true democracy and a better future of South Sudanese. The people of South Sudan deserve the latter.

Since the beginning of Israel’s offensive in the Gaza Strip in late 2023, Egypt has reviewed its security strategy, fearing that the conflict could spread to its borders. Cairo has significantly increased its military presence in the Sinai Peninsula.

Independent reports released last year indicated that Egypt had deployed more than 180 military battalions across the Sinai Peninsula, a number far exceeding the limits agreed upon under the Camp David Accords. The agreement allowed Egypt to maintain no more than 47 lightly armed battalions, with their deployment restricted mainly to the first security zone known as Zone A, which is closer to the Egyptian side near Cairo.

Regarding Egyptian military presence in Sinai, the agreement established strict restrictions. The Sinai Peninsula was divided into three zones (A, B, and C).

Zone A, located closest to Cairo, was the only area where Egypt was permitted to maintain a limited military presence.

Zone B, located in central Sinai, allowed Egypt to deploy border police equipped only with light weapons.

Zone C, located near the borders with Gaza and Israel, was designated as a demilitarized area, where Egypt was prohibited from stationing military forces.

Despite these restrictions, recent satellite images and leaked classified documents reportedly revealed that Egypt has built military airfields, underground defenses, and military bases in the area. These facilities allegedly include heavy weapons such as modern Abrams battle tanks and deployed air-defense systems, suggesting that Egypt may be exceeding the limitations established under the Camp David Accords.

Egypt views Israel’s military operations in the Gaza Strip and its reported intentions to reach the eastern border area of the Gaza Strip, which is adjacent to Egypt’s territory, as a threat to its national security. Cairo has therefore been closely monitoring Israeli military movements.

At the same time, Israel is focusing its attention on closely observing Egypt’s military expansion and capabilities in order to prevent further growth of Egyptian military power, which Tel Aviv considers a serious security concern.

All of these developments are occurring at a time when the region is experiencing a difficult crossroads, with rapid and unpredictable changes taking place.

Subject: Rejection of False Claims and Deliberate Historical Distortion Regarding Lake No (Dhoor) and Miach Payam

By Kuaidit Mijok Deng, Son of Ruweng Administrative Area and Lake No County

I wish to express my deep concern regarding the recent misleading narratives and unfounded claims about the history, identity, and administrative status of Lake No (Dhoor) and Miach Payam. As a son of the Ruweng Administrative Area and Lake No County, I consider it my duty to stand firmly for truth, historical accuracy, and peaceful coexistence.

I strongly condemn any attempt by individuals or groups to distort history, misrepresent facts, or deny the long-established presence and rights of communities that have lived in these areas for generations. History is not a matter of opinion, propaganda, or political convenience. It is rooted in documented facts, lived experiences, and collective memory that cannot be erased by statements, declarations, or social media campaigns.

It is unfortunate that some individuals continue to promote divisive narratives that lack historical evidence and legal foundation. Such actions do not promote peace, development, or unity. Instead, they create unnecessary tension, foster mistrust among neighboring communities, and undermine the spirit of brotherhood that our people have maintained despite many challenges.

It must be clearly understood that no individual, association, or interest group has the authority to rewrite history or deny the rights and existence of others. Facts remain unchanged regardless of whether they are accepted. Historical truth cannot be altered by repeating falsehoods or by political rhetoric.

I therefore call upon all responsible leaders, youth, and community members to reject misinformation and embrace constructive engagement based on truth, mutual respect, and the rule of law. Matters concerning land, boundaries, and community relations should be addressed through established institutions, historical records, and genuine dialogue rather than through inflammatory public statements that provoke division.

As a proud son of the Ruweng Administrative Area and Lake No County, I remain committed to peace, justice, and the preservation of historical truth. I firmly believe that our strength lies not in hostility toward one another but in our ability to resolve differences with wisdom, dignity, and respect for the facts.

To those who seek to distort history for personal or political gain, I offer this reminder: truth does not disappear because it is challenged, and history does not change because it is denied. Those who know their history will continue to defend it through lawful, peaceful, and principled means.

May we choose unity over division, truth over propaganda, and dialogue over confrontation for the benefit of present and future generations.

"History cannot be rewritten by declarations. Facts cannot be erased by opinions. Truth will always prevail, and peace will always remain our preferred path."

Issued by:
Kuaidit de Mijok Deng
Son of Ruweng Administrative Area and Lake No County

PUBLIC STATEMENT

OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER FOR DOMESTIC TAX REVENUE DIVISION
South Sudan Revenue Authority (SSRA)

The Office of the Commissioner for Domestic Tax Revenue Division has noted the circulation on social media of an alleged “Press Release” purporting the relief of Hon. Ambassador Muon Deng Ajuet as Commissioner General of the South Sudan Revenue Authority and the appointment of various individuals, including my name, to that position.

The public is advised to disregard these documents in their entirety. They do not exhibit the characteristics of an authentic government appointment instrument. A clear indication that they are fabricated is that the same document has been circulated in multiple versions, each bearing identical formatting, signatures, stamps, dates and reference numbers, but naming different individuals as the purported appointee. Such inconsistencies demonstrate that the documents have been altered and cannot all be genuine. This pattern is consistent with digitally manipulated or AI-generated content.

The apparent objective of these fabricated documents is to create confusion, undermine public confidence, and sow unnecessary division within the leadership of the South Sudan Revenue Authority, thereby providing opportunities for individuals seeking to exploit uncertainty for personal or political gain.

I therefore call upon the public, taxpayers, stakeholders, and development partners to remain calm and continue to support the leadership of Hon. Ambassador Muon Deng Ajuet and the entire management of the South Sudan Revenue Authority as they carry out their statutory mandate of assessing, collecting, and remitting government revenue to the Ministry of Finance and Planning.

The South Sudan Revenue Authority remains committed to professionalism, institutional integrity, and uninterrupted service to the people of South Sudan. The public is encouraged to rely only on official government communication channels for information relating to presidential appointments and institutional leadership.

Ustaz Ajang Ajang Lino
Commissioner for Domestic Tax Revenue Division
South Sudan Revenue Authority (SSRA)

SOUTH SUDAN SALVATION MOVEMENT (SSSM)
REVIVE • RENEW • RISE

PRESS STATEMENT

1. The wealth generated from South Sudan's oil sector has failed to serve the South Sudanese public. The tragic economic reality today is that the bulk of these oil revenues no longer flow into state coffers. Instead, the state continues to systematically divert crude oil cargoes to satisfy opaque debts manufactured by foreign creditors who help the very kleptocratic networks that loot our national funds. Now that the Juba regime has emptied the oil sector through state-sponsored financial mismanagement, it has found itself and its well-connected enablers left with no options, but to aggressively turn their attention to the country's remaining critical resources: our gold, diamonds and gemstones.

2. The recent aggressive grabbing of Bongo Community land in Tonj South County of Warrap State, for gold mining, is the latest action in a systematic campaign designed to strip South Sudan bare of its valuable minerals. The operation in Bongo Land is a flagrant violation of constitutional, statutory and community protections.

(a) The ongoing mining activities have not obtained the prior consent of the indigenous Bongo Community. The green light allegedly given by a tiny group of Bongo elites for the project to go ahead, does not amount to community consent and approval.

(b) The operation totally disregards the appropriate legal and regulatory procedures mandated by the Mining Act and national environmental protection laws.

(c) The well-connected and powerful individuals undertaking this mining activity have no moral legitimacy. They rely exclusively on the brute coercive power of the state to enforce their illegal occupation and extract wealth by force.

3. (a) The South Sudan Salvation Movement (SSSM) demands an immediate and absolute halt to all ongoing exploration and mining activities in the territory of the Bongo Community of Tonj South County. All mining equipment and affiliated personnel must be withdrawn without delay.

(b) We call for an independent and transparent investigation into the allocation of mining concessions in Warrap State, including the full disclosure of the identities behind the domestic and foreign entities involved in the Tonj South operations.

(c) No future mineral exploration anywhere in South Sudan should be allowed to proceed without full compliance with statutory regulatory procedures, comprehensive environmental and social impacts assessments and the verified written consent of the local communities.

4. The (SSSM) stands in absolute solidarity with the Bongo Community of Tonj South County and calls upon all patriotic citizens, civil society organizations and international transparency watchdogs to join us in resisting this localized resource grab in Tonj South County and Greater Tonj Area of Warrap State, and the wider plunder of South Sudan's sovereign wealth by the very custodians we have entrusted to safeguard it.

The wealth of South Sudan belongs to the generations of South Sudan and not to a kleptocratic few.

THE PLUNDER MUST STOP NOW.

Signed:

Nhial Deng Nhial
Chairman, South Sudan Salvation Movement (SSSM)

EXPOSE: Deputy First Lady Gregory Vasili – The Undersecretary Weaponizing Government Power to Kill Innocent South Sudanese for his personal gains

A direct call to President Salva Kiir Mayardit: Remove this man before he destroys the nation.

The Undersecretary for Defense in South Sudan’s Ministry of Defense and Veterans Affairs, General Gregory Vasili, also known as Deng Kuac Aduol, is actively engineering communal violence between communities in Warrap State and Western Bahr el Ghazal State. This is not speculation. This is fact.

Gregory is not a peacemaker. He is a killer wearing a government uniform.

The Massacre at Dawn – June 14, 2026

In the early hours of June 14, 2026, a group of armed youth from the Apuk community in Warrap State, acting under direct instructions from Gregory Vasili, launched a brutal night attack on innocent civilians of the Marial Wau community in Western Bahr el Ghazal State.

These were not soldiers. These were farmers – men, women, and elders – sleeping peacefully or already working on their own land at dawn.

The result: More than 16 people were killed on their own farms. Their bodies left in the soil they had cultivated. Their cattle – their life savings, their children’s future – were stolen by Gregory’s armed group from Apuk.

This was not a spontaneous tribal clash. This was a planned, armed assault ordered by a senior government official.

The False Peace Mission – A Cover for ochestrating communal violence

Gregory Vasili recently traveled from Juba to his home village in Apuk. He announced publicly that his mission was peace – that he intended to reconcile with old political friends from Apuk with whom he had fallen out long ago.

Behind the mask of reconciliation, Gregory used the visit to mobilize Apuk youth for communal violence. Our underground reporter has informed us that gregory and other Apuk general gathered Apuk armed youth in a secret meetings held in his Luonyaker resident. In the meeting, he revived old grievances. He pointed his finger across the border to the Marial Wau community and gave his orders: "Attack them, Drive them out, this is our land" Gregory stated in the meeting

He specifically targeted three small but fertile areas: Manyang, Wun Ngot, and Mabior Abun. These are disputed lands where both communities have lived and farmed for years. But Gregory wants them for himself.

Why? Land. Greed. Power.

Gregory Vasili wants to own that land. He wants to turn it into his personal farm. Everyone knows these areas are fertile, some of the best farmland in the region. Gregory saw an opportunity. Instead of buying land or negotiating, he chose to kill the inhabitants.

He is chasing innocent people off their ancestral farms so he can plant his own crops. That is the depth of his corruption and cruelty.

Guns and Ammunition – Stolen from the Army

Here is the most dangerous part of this crime: Gregory did not use civilian weapons. He used the power of the state.

Recently when he when he went to Apuk, he was carrying a bulky of guns and ammunitions he is supplying to  local youth of Apuk. To deflect the attention, he claimed these weapons belonged to SSPDF Division 11, which is stationed in Apuk. Officially, he said the arms were destined for the military barracks, so they were given the pass, but that never happened.

Instead, under cover of darkness, Gregory’s men distributed the guns and ammunition to selected sections of Apuk youth. The military supplies never reached any barracks which they were intended to. They went straight into the hands of Apuk militias he controls.

This means a senior Undersecretary for Defense is arming civilians with government weapons to attack other South Sudanese civilians. He is using the army’s own resources to wage a private war for little land he want to cultivate.

The Political Connection – Protection from the Top

Gregory Vasili is not just any general. He is the brother of the First Lady of South Sudan. He is also an in‑law to President Salva Kiir Mayardit. Many people called him deputy first lady due to his closeness to the first lady

That family connection has likely protected him for years. But it must not protect him from this.

He is using his position – and his relationship to the presidency – as a shield. He believes no one can touch him. He believes he can kill, steal land, arm militias, and walk back to Juba without consequence.

This is exactly why President Kiir must act now.

A Direct Appeal to President Kiir

Mr. President:

Gregory Vasili is not serving your government. He is destroying it. Every weapon he hands out, every life he takes, every community he sets against another – that blood is on your administration’s hands if you do nothing.

He went home pretending to make peace with his political rivals. Instead, he made war. Sixteen innocent farmers are dead. Families have lost their cattle, their land, their loved ones. Entire communities in Western Bahr el Ghazal now live in fear – not of rebels, but of your own Undersecretary for Defense.

If Gregory is allowed to stay, you send one clear message: Government officials can kill with impunity. Army weapons can be given to militias. Land can be taken by force.

That message will tear South Sudan apart.

The Time for Action Is Now

We do not ask for investigation. We do not ask for dialogue. The evidence is clear. The dead are buried. The stolen cattle are gone. The guns are already in the villages.

We demand only one thing: Remove Gregory Vasili immediately.

Stripe him of his rank. Arrest him. Try him for incitement to violence, murder, and theft of military property. And send a clear warning to every other official who thinks they can use state power for personal gain.

Mr. President, you have the power to stop this. Use it. Before more innocent blood soaks the soil of Warrap and Western Bahr el Ghazal. Before Gregory’s greed starts a war that consumes the entire region.

Remove him. Now.

A powerful political storm is quietly gathering strength in South Sudan, one orchestrated by Hon. Atong Kuol Manyang. Her first and most dangerous objective is to dismantle the South Sudan People's Defense Forces (SSPDF) from within. By creating false narratives, she hopes to orchestrate the dismissal of Kiir's most capable commanders, fostering a deep and paralyzing distrust between the president and his own army. TITLE: SOUTH SUDAN’S “COOL WAR”: WHEN PEACE BECOMES MORE DANGEROUS THAN BULLETS.

June,12/2026

By Simon Yai Deng | Student of International Relations & Diplomacy, Diploma holder in Accounting & Finance.

SUBHEAD: We survived the hot war of guns. But are we losing the cool war of systems?

We were taught as children that war is loud. War is gunfire at night. War is running from your home with only your life.

We survived that war. We signed peace. We raised flag🇸🇸🕊️. We said “Never Again.”

But since from 2013 to present , many South Sudanese are asking a painful question: Did the war really end, or did it just change uniforms?

As a student of International Relations and Diplomacy, I have learned there are two types of war:

1. HOT WAR: The War We All See
Hot war is bullets, tanks, and displacement. It is CNN, UN reports, and refugee camps. It is dangerous, yes. But it is honest. In hot war, the enemy wears a uniform. In hot war, citizens unite. In hot war, the world sends aid and says “We see you.”

2. COOL WAR: The War We Don’t Name
Cool war is silence. It is hardship designed into systems. No bombs drop, but dreams die daily.
Cool war is:
>Salary delays for a quiet times while inflation eats what’s left. That’s not “economic delay”. That’s economic violence. It makes a teacher, nurse, or soldier powerless in his own country.
>Hospitals without medicine, schools without education (qualify teachers). When the state cannot heal the sick or teach the child, it sends one message: “Citizen, you are on your own.” People don’t become “nothing” overnight. They are made to feel like nothing, slowly.
>Youth with degrees but no dignity.  We graduate with Diplomas, Bachelor’s degrees, Master’s degrees and remain unemployed because in South Sudan many job opportunities depend on who you know, then wait years for a chance. Cool war doesn’t kill the body. It kills ambition. And a nation without ambitious youth is a nation preparing for its next hot war.

THE DANGEROUS BELIEF
People believe hot war is the only dangerous war. So we fear gunfire more than we fear empty clinics. We protest bullets more than we question broken systems.

But IR teaches me: Cool war kills more, because it kills hope first, then people. Hot war makes headlines. Cool war makes orphans of the future. By the time we notice, an entire generation already feels like “nothing” to those in power.

MY CONSTRUCTIVE APPEAL AS A STUDENT, NOT AN ENEMY
I write this not as an opposition voice, but as a son of this soil. My criticism is patriotism, not treason.

To our leaders: Your legacy will not be measured by how well you survived war. It will be measured by how well you built peace. Peace is not just the absence of gunfire. Peace is the presence of salary on time, medicine in hospitals, jobs for graduates, and dignity for every citizen.

Stop the cool war by design. Build systems that make citizens feel like owners, not strangers, in South Sudan. Because a government that makes its youth feel invisible today… will have no youth to defend it tomorrow.

CLOSING TRUTH
In scripture: “You shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free.”
In diplomacy: Truth, told with wisdom, builds nations.

South Sudan does not need more silence. We need more courage — the courage of leaders to fix systems, and the courage of citizens to speak truth without fear.

The hot war took our past. Let us not allow the cool war to steal our future.

The author is a South Sudanese citizen and a forth year student of International Relations & Diplomacy, SIU, Diploma holder in Accounting & Finance, CVI. He writes on governance, youth, and national development.

According to sources, several South Sudanese subcontractors whose contracts were reportedly reassigned through a single-source process to Sudanese businessman Mohaned Ahmed raised complaints with the newly appointed GPOC Vice President, Eng. Biem Thonchar. The subcontractors reportedly questioned decisions that they believe were made under the tenure of former Undersecretary Dr. Chol Deng.

Sources claim that after receiving the complaints, Eng. Biem Thonchar sought clarification from the CD Manager regarding the matter. During the discussion, the Vice President reportedly instructed that the issue be presented before the Management Committee (MC) for review and determination of the legality and propriety of the contracting decisions.

However, according to the same sources, information about the internal discussion appeared on social media the following day in a different form. The posts allegedly claimed that the Vice President intended to award contracts to Deng Wal, Executive Director in the Office of the President.

The Management Committee is described as the company’s principal decision-making and oversight body, comprising representatives of partner companies, security managers, and departmental heads.

Sources further allege that officials aligned with the former Undersecretary are concerned that the disputed contract awards may not withstand scrutiny before the Management Committee and are therefore engaging in a campaign of misinformation.

‎Hon. Adut Salva Kiir isn't a scapegoat for Gaddafi's owned crime: Respond to The Kapital Press, Garang John and other Media platforms.

By the Gate Way Press 
‎
‎The concerted propaganda and character assassination attempt by The Kapital Press, Garang John, and other media platforms to frame Hon. Adut Salva Kiir as a scapegoat for crimes committed by Gaddafi is a fabricated distortion that collapses under minimal scrutiny. Let it be clear: no amount of political maneuvering will transfer Gaddafi’s own criminal liabilities onto an innocent public servant. Gaddafi must carry his own cross—alone and fully accountable for his actions.
‎
‎Gaddafi stands as an illegal citizen of two different countries, having established a pattern of criminal conduct in both Kenya and South Sudan. The documented offenses he committed across these jurisdictions are his alone to answer for. To suggest otherwise—to imply that Hon. Adut had any hand in directing or facilitating his crimes—is not only false but a deliberate diversion from the core facts of the case.
‎
‎There exists no evidence, credible or otherwise, that Hon. Adut Salva Kiir ever sent Gaddafi to work on her behalf. No cooperative business relationship ever existed between them. The baseless claims that his arrest relates in any way to Crawford Capital lack a single shred of supporting evidence, rendering them entirely unworthy of belief. These assertions are invented narratives designed to weaponize another man’s wrongdoing against a blameless figure.
‎
‎Hon. Adut Salva Kiir is not a general in the security sector. Her official position is Presidential Advisor on Special Programs—a portfolio squarely focused on national development, infrastructure, humanitarian coordination, and economic planning, not security operations. The deliberate misrepresentation of her role is a transparent tactic to manufacture a connection where none exists, solely to shield Gaddafi from the full weight of his own crimes.
‎
‎Turning to Garang John, the facts speak harshly.

text:
An Urgent Appeal for Peace and Unity

By Deng Diu Cyierdit alias Deng Bigdeal  

To the Dinka and Nuer communities,

It is imperative that we address the senseless violence and raids plaguing our communities. The conflict between our tribes has led to devastating consequences, claiming innocent lives and destroying livelihoods.

We must recognize the distinction between political differences and the citizens who bear the brunt of these conflicts. The politicians and leaders who once fought alongside us are now seated in offices, while our brothers and sisters continue to suffer.

We implore you: let us put aside our differences and work toward a brighter future. The citizens of South Sudan deserve peace, stability, and prosperity. It is time to silence the guns and foster understanding. The only thing I have understood from our fellow citizens is that they do not reason about why they fight each other.

Let us choose unity over division and work together to build a nation where every individual can thrive.

Ezekiel Lol Gatkuoth and Ateny Wek Ateny's inflammatory and divisive remarks are disgraceful, unprofessional, and detrimental to peace and national cohesion in our country. President Salva Kiir Mayardit, or Presidential Special Envoy, Hon. Adut Kiir, should consider removing these two individuals from public office.

The two prodigal sons, Ateny Wek Ateny and Ezekiel Lol Gatkuoth, are unfit to continue serving as public figures in the Republic of South Sudan.

These two politicians (prodigal sons) have consistently demonstrated attitudes and rhetoric that threaten diversity, unity, and peaceful coexistence. Their actions and statements have been closely observed over the years, yet their continued presence in government adds little value to nation-building and reconciliation efforts.

South Sudan's painful experience in 2013 and 2016 should serve as a reminder of the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric. The 2013 conflict erupted following political tensions and mistrust within the SPLM leadership, which quickly escalated into deadly violence between forces aligned with Dr. Riek Machar and those defending President Salva Kiir's government. Similarly, the 2016 fighting in Juba demonstrated how hostile political narratives, ethnic polarization, and reckless public statements can deepen divisions and trigger armed confrontations. Furthermore, the spread of hate speech and accusations against political opponents has historically fueled fear, mistrust, and retaliation among communities, contributing to instability and loss of life.

Public officials should promote dialogue, reconciliation, and national unity rather than engage in rhetoric that risks reopening old wounds or undermining the fragile peace that South Sudanese citizens continue to seek and defend.

BREAKING: “My Loyalty Was Repaid With Chains: Gen. Stephen Buay on Arrest, Humiliation and Exile".

HOW I WAS BETRAYED BY THE SPLM-NCP;

BY GEN: STEPHEN BUOY ROLNYANG. 
————————————————————————————-

After President Museveni and I saved him from being toppled by his former Vice President Riek Machar Teny-Dhurgon, President Kiir ordered his Chief of Defence Staff, General Gabriel Jok Riak to arrest and fly me from Mayom County to Juba in handcuffs on May 31, 2018.

I was attacked in Mayom town on May 31, 2018, around 1200 hours by pro-government Mayom-based militias under the direct command of Major General Mathew Puljang Top. Three soldiers were killed, and two others wounded among my personal bodyguards who were accompanying me home. I did not fight in self-defence because it was not my intention to do anything stupid that would be used against me in a court of law. 

They arrested, shackled, and flew me to Juba the following day by a small caravan plane. On arrival at Juba International Airport, I was manhandled and thrown into a small national security van that did not have any ventilation, save for a few small holes created to let in some air. They threw me in an old underground bunker that was initially used as a torture chamber in Juba by the former Sudan military intelligence during the war to throw in and lynch suspected South Sudanese who were accused of being SPLA supporters. When Sudan Armed Forces withdrew to the North, the bunker became a dwelling ground for snakes, rats, and other harmful and poisonous creatures. 

The South Sudan People's Defence Forces (SSPDF) Military intelligence instead converted it for the same use against the South Sudanese accused of opposing President Kir's regime. Many South Sudanese People, especially from Dinka Awiel, Nuer and Equatorians have been lynched and tortured secretly in that bunker. Decomposed bodies could be smelt inside the bunker that is 4 by 8 meters long.

I was bundled into the bunker for three days with my legs and hands shackled and without food and water. I was forced to sleep on the rough floor and struggled to safety whenever I spotted a snake or a rat charging towards me in the dark, rolling on my belly from one side of the bunker to the other. I urinated in my pants for three days until when I was transferred from military intelligence custody under a cruel military intelligence officer, Brigadier General Kuel Garang Kuel to Military Police cells where the handcuffs were broken and removed because there were no keys to unlock them. 

The keys were thrown into a toilet by Brigadier Kuel Garang Kuel fearing that the handcuffs would be removed by his soldiers in his absence because the soldiers manning the custody were not happy with the way! was being humiliated despite being a comrade and the one who served and commanded various SPLA (SSPDF) units. "According to the South Sudan interim laws, "an accused person is presumed not guilty until proven in the court of law".

On June 16, 2018, the Chief of Defence Forces formed an investigation committee under Major General Late Michael Manok Kot to investigate my alleged rebellion against the government and whether I was in contact with the rebel leader General Paul Malong Awan. The charges were framed by Major General Mathew Puljang Top himself and politicians of my home area Bul Nuer, especially Tut Keaw Gatluak and Joseph Manytuil, the Governor of Unity State to get rid of me politically and physically. 

The committee recommended to the former Chief of Defence Staff General Gabriel Jok Riak that they did not find me guilty of the alleged offences and suggested that I should be released immediately. However, the Chief of Defence Staff was very furious with the committee's outcome, and he ordered the committee to sit again and investigate further until they must find me guilty.

The committee upon being forced to redo the investigation conducted a fresh investigation and assumed that they found me guilty and recommended that I should be arraigned in a General Court Martial (GCM) to answer the charges.

On January 3, 2019, the Chief of Defence Staff formed a General Court Martial that consisted of seven members namely:

1. Major Gen Thik Achiek Hol-
Court President

2. Brig. Gen Riak Tiop Deng -
Member

3. Brig. Gen Duol Gony—Member

4. Brig. Gen Nhial Arou—Member

5. Brig. Gen Angui Geng —Member

6. Brig. Gen Hillery Oduho—Member

7. Brig. Gen Abubakar Mohamed—Member

On February 4, 2019, I appeared before the General Court Martial and was asked if I had any objection to the formation of the members of the panel. I told the court that I had a reservation with the whole panel due to the following reasons:

Firstly, the SPLA Act 2009, Article 35 (4) says, in all cases, the presiding officer shall be senior in rank to the accused and that all members of the panel be at least equivalent in rank to the accused. Therefore, in my case, the presiding officer should have been a Lieutenant General and six Major Generals.

Secondly, the SPLA Act 2009, Article 36(2), says that the General Court Martial shall be convened by the Commander-in-Chief when the person being tried is in the rank of a Brigadier General and above and the Chief of Defence Staff should convene a court in respect of other junior officers in the lower ranks. The court had been wrongly constituted and had to be dissolved in conformity with the above legal procedures. The General Court-martial was dissolved, and the Chief of Defence Staff recommended new names to the Commander-in-Chief to reconstitute a new General Court Martial, which the President reconstituted hereunder:

1. Major Gen Thik Achiek Hol-
Court President

2. Major Gen Atem Duot Atem -
Member

3. Major Gen Peter Gatwech Gai-l
Member

4. Major Gen Akuei Ajou Akuei-
Member

5. Major Gen Isiah Paul Lotole -
Member

6. Brig. Gen Abubakar Mohamed - Judge Advocate

The court conducted 17 sessions upon which it collected views and facts from the witnesses. The last session was held at a closed-door where closing arguments and mitigations were held. The court dropped some of the charges such as Article 60 which related to treason and Article 61 for offences relating to security that had been levelled against me earlier.

The only charge that remained was, disobeying lawful orders from your superior that were found in Article 67 and Standing Orders Article 69, SPLA Act 2009. I was not given a fair trial because the General Court Martial was politically manipulated and received incentives in the form of bribery at the end of every session from the very people who masterminded my arrest.

It is worth mentioning that, at the end of every session, a vehicle with the Presidential numberless plate from the house of the Presidential Security Advisor Tut Keaw Gatluak could be seen openly coming to the court to pick up some members of the GCM and dropping them at their respective homes.

They could be seen giving a copy of that day's session to the driver of Tut Keaw Gatluak to take it to him so that he was informed about the day's court session. This had been continuing until when there was a serious tie vote among the members of the martial court because there was no substantial evidence found, that could be used to convict me. However, the tie was simply broken because of rampant poverty in South Sudan since the members of the GCM were bribed with hundreds of US dollars, according to one of the persons whom I will not mention here, who was among the team that went and paid the money to some powerful members among the members of the GCM who could influence the whole court.

The General Court Martial was forced to break a tie and improvised an arbitrary decision based on available administrative articles such as Article 67 "disobeying of lawful orders from your superior" and Article 69 "standing orders" SPLA Act 2009, which are very administrative and only can be applied in the case involving a junior SPLA personnel.

Therefore, the court martial endorsed the following ruling:

1. Demoted me from the rank of Major General to Private.

2. Dismissed me from the SSPDF as a civilian.

3. Sentenced me to one-year imprisonment from the date of my arrest on May 31, 2018, which elapsed during the trial.

After reading out the ruling, the General Court Martial asked me whether I would like to appeal against the verdict, which I turned down as there was nowhere, I could appeal against the verdict because the same powerful people who influenced and manipulated the decision of the court could also do the same in the outcome of my appeal. I gave up and left everything as it was decided by the General Court Martial and instead made the following statement: -

Honourable Court, when I moved from Wau to my home in Mayom, I asked for permission from the Commander of the Ground Forces on phone, who gave me five days and directed that immediately proceed to Wau and hand over the command of 5t Infantry Division to the new Commander once / am back from my home.

The Commander of the Ground Forces came to this Honourable Court and denied that he did not grant me permission to go home. I requested this Honourable Court to contact the Mobile Telecommunication Company (MTN) to provide this Honourable Court with my audio contact with the Commander of the Ground Forces, but this Honourable Court turned down my request in favour of the Commander of the Ground Forces.

I talked with the Commander-in-Chief, President Salva Kir, in Mayom on the phone of General Akol Koor on the allegations that reached the President's office that I wanted to defect and join the rebels. But when the Commander-in-Chief found out that the allegations were not true and that I only went home to offer traditional sacrifices on my father's grave, the Commander-in-Chief himself gave me five more days to spend at home before going back to Wau. The Commander-in-Chief told me that he would inform the Chief of Defence Staff that he had given me five more days to spend at home in Bieh-Nyang Payam.

I was attacked by Major General Mathew Puljang - I thought with orders from the SSPDF headquarters - and his soldiers killed three of my bodyguards and wounded two others. Interestingly, you have not arrested or demoted him to a private like what you have just done to me, yet I did not fight back because I knew that they are the government forces and I had to surrender to them knowing that they might have been ordered by the SSPDF headquarters to arrest me. It has appeared in this honourable court that nobody ordered Major General Mathew Puljang from the SSPDF to attack and arrest me. Major General Puljang was acting on his own without being ordered by the SSPDF headquarters to do so, but to my surprise, no action was taken against him by the SSPDF command. 

Instead, I am the one who has been arrested and charged with treason and other charges, while Major General Puljang was the one who killed three of my bodyguards and wounded two others, yet we did not fight them back in self-defence. Therefore, Mathew Puljang Top should be charged with murder. If I had fought Major General Mathew Puljang in self-defence, I wouldn't have been arrested as there would have been a lot of deaths on both sides in Mayom town, that is why my soldiers were only the ones killed and wounded in cold blood simply because / did not fight back.
Honourable Court, the verdict that you have just passed on me, is a one-year imprisonment sentence starting from the date of my arrest on May 31, 2018, which elapsed last May 2019, yet you are keeping me in jail. This is very humiliating to my personality.

Honourable Court, this case is politically motivated by a few politicians from my own community Bul Nuer who are conspiring and colluding with the Chief of Defence Staff to get rid of me politically and physically.

Therefore, I feel betrayed by these politicians and officers from my community in the face of the SSPDF command despite the immense contribution that / have made in defence of this country and its constitution. END OF MY STATEMENT!

The decision of the General Court Martial was supposed to be taken to the President for confirmation according to Article 89 (2), SPLA Act 2009, that states "the findings and sentence of a General Court Martial (GCM), shall be confirmed by the President and Commander-in-chief. In my case, the President did not confirm the decision of the General Court Martial, nor did he delegate a warrant to anyone to do so on his behalf or announced any Presidential decree on the South Sudan Broadcasting Corporation (SSBC) National TV as would be the case of a senior officer like I am.

It is worth mentioning that, the legal advisor in the office of the President the late Molana Majok Mading connived with Honourable Tut Keaw Gatluak and General Gabriel Jok Riak not to submit the decision of the General Court Martial to the President for confirmation, because of some legal irregularities involved in the court procedures which were likely to be in my favour if it were submitted to the President who would be much obliged by the law to dismiss the case altogether. They went ahead and announced the decision of the General Court-martial at a military parade in Bilpam (SPF HQ) because the late Molana Majok Mading wrote to the Chief of Defence Staff in his capacity as legal advisor in the office of the President giving a greenlight to announce the judgement without any warrant signed by the President himself to confirm my conviction.

They went and briefed the President about what they had done illegally and by telling the people that the President was so busy with other national issues that he could not sign the confirmation letter by himself. The President kept quiet without reacting to the illegality of the announcement, instead the President told them to wait and see any negative reaction from the public or army so that he would pretend as if he was not aware of what was going on in the General Court Martial and he would eventually try to dismiss the case if things go wrong in the public or within the army.

Below is the letter written to the Chief of Defence Staff by the late Justice Majok Mading to give a green light to the Chief of Defence Staff to make the pronouncement of my conviction at a military parade ground as planned by the Chief of Defence Staff and Honourable Tut Keaw Gatluak. The letter reads as follows:

"Subject: Confirmation of the Verdict of General Court Martial (GCM) Verdict on Criminal Case No. 22/2018 of Maj. Gen. Stephen Buoy Rolnyang. I refer to the referenced letter Number GCM/J/351/2019, from the President of the General Court Martial Maj. Gen. Thiik Aciek Hol dated 21 October 2019, addressed to H.E. the President and Commander-in-Chief of the SSPDF, in which the General Court Martial (GCM) read out the verdict to the above-mentioned convict.

According to the documents on record, and after the court ruling, the convict was asked whether he wished to exercise his right of appeal or not in accordance with the provisions of Section 88 (2) of the SPLA Act, 2009, read together with Section 263 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, 2008. The convict is on record as having been satisfied by the verdict and hence did not intend to appeal.

Therefore, HE. the President has confirmed the verdict of the General Court-martial (GCM) in totality, and he has further directed that the convict should be released forthwith".

Have the assurance of my highest regards and consideration,

Molana Majok Mading, Legal Advisor, Office of the President.

After was released from jail, I happily joined my family and stayed at home for three years and later decided to register and establish a security firm called Jamus Security Service (JSS) in Juba, at least to support my family financially so that could no longer depend on the government support. When there was a contest for the position of the Governor of Unity State, I decided to submit my application to the office of the SPLM with the intention to be appointed to the position based on a popular demand from the people of Unity State to serve them as their governor to reconcile them, restore peace and rebuild the much-needed beautiful social fabrics, harmony and co-existence that used to be among the communities of Western Upper Nile that were destroyed by the SPLM infighting.

Unfortunately, when some powerful members of the Sudan People Liberation Movement and National Congress Party (SPLM-NCP) found out that my application for the governorship position had reached the office of the SPLM and my name was about to be shortlisted and subsequently presented to the President for final endorsement, they went and talked to the former SPLM Secretary General Nunu Kumba and paid her handsomely and Kumba immediately removed my name in favour of Joseph Nguen Manytuil. 

They re-appointed Joseph Nguen Manytuil as the Governor for an indefinite period while doing nothing for the people of Unity State. Instead, he is discriminating and kills the people of Unity State on clan lines. This is demonstrated in what has been going on in the South of Unity State areas of Koch, Leer and Mayendit, where thousands of people have been displaced and villages burnt down. The violence has also seen the killing of children and elderly people who could not run for their lives and all other forms of evil acts including gender-based violence.

The SPLM-NCP quest to get rid of me did not stop there. They had planned to assassinate me when Joseph Manytuil was finally re-appointed as the Governor of Unity State. The population of Unity State reacted negatively and protested, but in vain against the reappointment of Joseph Nguen Manytuil as the governor of Unity State. The SPLM-NCP concluded that it was me who instigated the people of Unity State to protest the reappointment of Joseph Nguen Manytuil. They then onwards, staged several assassination attempts on me but failed because I maintained a low profile in Juba. Breaking News: AU-backed talks with South Sudan opposition underway in Tanzania

High-level consultative meetings involving South Sudan opposition groups are underway in Dar El Salaam, Tanzania, as part of efforts to revive an inclusive peace process amid stalled implementation of the 2018 peace agreement.

The consultations are being held under the auspices of former Tanzanian president and African Union envoy on South Sudan, Jakaya Kikwete.

The meetings, which are being conducted separately with each group, began on Thursday and are expected to conclude on Friday.

Participants include:

1. the United People’s Alliance (UPA), led by Pagan Amum.

2. the South Sudan Opposition Movements Alliance (SSOMA), led by Gen. Thomas Cirillo.

3. the country’s second-largest party, SPLM-IO, led by Dr. Riek Machar.

4. the People’s Coalition for Civil Action (PCCA).

5. the Federal Democratic Party, led by Gabriel Changson Chang.

Speaking to Radio African Press on Thursday, UPA Secretary General Lual Dau said the group’s delegation, led by Amum, was taking part in consultations with the AU team.

The UPA high-level delegation includes:

1. Gen. Paul Malong Awan.
2. Gen. Marko Laku.
3. Gen. Stephen Buay Rolnyang.
4. Gen. Oyai Deng Ajak.
5. Dr. Cirino Hiteng and other members,” Lual said.

Lual said the opposition groups had presented their views on the failure to fully implement the revitalised peace agreement, the government’s withdrawal from the Tumaini Peace Initiative, and violations of the peace deal.

“We proposed that the only way forward for an inclusive peace process is to begin with the release of all political detainees in the country and the return of all parties to an inclusive dialogue to draw a clear roadmap for peace,” he said.

He said the consultations were intended to help the AU better understand the political and security situation in South Sudan and gather the opposition’s views on challenges facing the country and possible pathways to peace.

Lual said the talks followed earlier consultations held by Kikwete in Juba, where he met government officials and political parties.

“After these meetings, AU envoy Kikwete will have the full picture on how to address the challenges of South Sudan and how best he can approach issues of peace in South Sudan,” Lual said.

Gai Mayen Luk, a senior SPLM-IO member, said the group had sent two representatives to attend the meetings after what he described as an initial misunderstanding over the invitation was resolved.

“We have sent Hon. Gatluak Gabriel Deng and Hon. Gatluak Michael. They are already in Dar es Salaam for the consultative meetings,” Mayen said.

A PCCA member, who declined to be named, confirmed the group had met Kikwete on Thursday and briefed him on challenges surrounding implementation of previous peace agreements.

The official said the group urged the AU to mobilise regional and international support for an inclusive dialogue process and ensure accountability for violations of peace agreements.

“If the AU does not have a strong voice, peace will not prevail in South Sudan,” he said.

Kikwete visited Juba in early April on a three-day fact-finding mission during which he met President Salva Kiir and political parties based in the capital.

Kikwete, Tanzania’s fourth president from 2005 to 2015, was appointed in March by the African Union chairperson as High Representative for the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, with a special mandate on South Sudan.

The consultations fall under the African Union’s Ad Hoc High-Level Committee on South Sudan, known as the C5, which supports implementation of the 2018 peace agreement and promotes inclusive dialogue ahead of elections.

In February, the C5 called for measures including elections in December 2026, the release of detainees, particularly Machar, inclusive dialogue among parties, and a ceasefire.

A Mindful Response to a national employee in South Sudan oil sector Dr. Biem Deng's Reckless Statement against BB Energy Company 

This reckless statement which blindly constitutes attack against BB Energy Company reflects more emotion than facts. The language and accusations used are familiar and appear to echo comments previously associated with Dr. Biem Deng, a senior official in the oil sector. Repeating politically charged narratives without evidence and reposting them publicly without considering the consequences is reckless and irresponsible.

An employee working in the national oil sector must understand that personal opinions written for attention or salary interests do not automatically represent credible public policy positions or the realities of the petroleum industry. Public commentary should be guided by professionalism, evidence, and awareness of the wider impact such statements can have on the country’s reputation and investment climate.

Misleading claims about “corruption,” “blackmail,” and “political manipulation” without proof do not weaken BB Energy Company as much as they further damage confidence in South Sudan’s own oil sector. International investors observe these statements closely, and careless accusations create the impression of instability, internal hostility, and institutional disorder.

There are many examples globally where irresponsible public rhetoric harmed national industries more than foreign companies themselves:

1. In Nigeria, repeated politically motivated accusations against international oil companies discouraged investment and delayed critical energy projects, ultimately affecting local workers and government revenues more than the companies involved.

2. In Sudan and South Sudan’s own history, public disputes among officials and sector employees created uncertainty that weakened investor confidence and contributed to production disruptions.

3. In Venezuela, continuous political attacks against foreign energy partners resulted in reduced international cooperation, declining production capacity, and severe economic consequences for the nation itself.

Criticism of any company should be based on verified facts, legal processes, and institutional accountability — not recycled political talking points or emotional allegations. BB Energy’s contracts and operations should be judged through transparent legal and regulatory frameworks, not through reckless social media narratives designed to inflame public opinion.

Those working within the oil sector should focus on strengthening the credibility of the industry, not deepening mistrust and embarrassment through unsupported statements that ultimately implicate the entire sector more than any single company.

text:
A legitimate question from Ugandan security personnel triggered the chaotic incident involving President Salva Kiir Mayardit and his close bodyguards at Kololo Grounds in Kampala.

To those who are unaware about the truth behind the chaotic incident involving President Salva Kiir Mayardit's bodyguards and Ugandan security personnel, this statement is exactly for you so that you can understand the factors of the incident. On 12 May 2026 in Kampala, President Salva Kiir Mayardit and his delegation were present on an official visit to attend the inauguration of their key regional ally, the long-serving African leader, President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni known as the King of African politics. It was President Museveni’s swearing-in day as President of the Republic of Uganda.

At Kololo Grounds, a highly secured venue where the event took place, all Heads of State arrived smoothly and took their seats quietly, without attracting unusual public attention. However, when it was President Kiir’s turn, a protocol crisis began almost immediately.

Before leaving his residence, where he was staying with his designated successor, Hon. Adut Kiir, and other officials who had accompanied him, it had already been officially communicated that, in line with new security measures put in place by Uganda’s security sector for the event, President Kiir would be allowed into the venue with only four bodyguards and all their firearms msut disarmed as they enter Kololo Grounds. His Private Secretary and several other guards were required to remain at the residence, as security forces could not permit anything outside these established measures.

However, upon President Kiir’s arrival at Kololo Grounds, the number of accompanying bodyguards still appeared excessive, which heightened tensions. At the core of the incident was a question reportedly raised by two Ugandan security officers: “We are protecting President Kiir in Juba from powerful and aggressive South Sudanese rebels. Why do you think we cannot protect him here, in one of the safest and most secure cities, Kampala?” 

This remark appears to have provoked a strong reaction. In that moment, some of President Kiir’s younger bodyguards abandoned diplomatic restraint, and the situation devolved into a physical altercation, briefly turning part of Kololo Grounds into a scene of disorder where unusual confrontation quickly erupted between Kiir’s bodyguards and Ugandan security personnel, particularly members of the protocol unit. 
What followed was a rapid escalation of unpleasant looks at each other, pulling themselves, pushing, punching each other in a hateful manner, and unfriendly exchange of aggressive and disrespectful words. The bitterness on both sides was clearly visible as one bodyguard was heard telling the Ugandan side that "this is not Dr. John Garang".

Blame has since been directed at security personnel from both South Sudan and Uganda. However, others argue that ultimate responsibility of this incident lies with the leadership structure surrounding the South Sudanese presidency, especially the First Family particularly regarding their reliance on only Uganda military and security support for over 13 years now. Ugandan security personnel, in this view, were justified in raising concerns, given their long-standing role in supporting security and military operations in South Sudan, an arrangement that has itself been subject to political debate not only in South Sudan but across the World.

This account is based on information from multiple sources, including individuals close to Hon. Adut Kiir’s security detail and other reliable contacts who spoke directly with Hon. Ateny Wek Ateny regarding the matter.
