BREAKING NEWS: SSPM/A of Gen. Stephen Buay Rolnyang, Marks 5 Years,Declares Readiness for Confrontation and Rejects 2026 General Elections as "Sham"

5th Anniversary of the SSPM/A

Revolutionary Greetings!

Comrades-in-arms, gallant forces of the South Sudan People's Movement and Army (SSPM/A), and the courageous people of South Sudan, today we mark five years since the birth of our Movement. This anniversary is not merely a commemoration; it is a reaffirmation of our unbreakable commitment to the struggle for freedom, dignity, and justice.

Let us rise and honour our fallen heroes, whose blood waters the tree of liberation. Among them are Comrade Gatluak Majiok Liey, who was brutally and extrajudicially executed by the regime by burning him in a burning hut, and other comrades, Nyuon Garang Kuol, Pur Ruop Kuol and Dhoal Barpuoh Tap, who extrajudicially faced firing squads with courage and all the other comrades who have fallen in the process of the liberation struggle. Their sacrifice is the flame that lights our path forward 

On the 1 of May 2021, the SSPM/A was born out of necessity to rescue our people from dictatorial rule, the politics of tribalism, corruption, nepotism, and patronage, and to restore dignity, justice, and unity to our nation, in which the SSPM/A has set three phases of struggle for the past five years:

Phase-1: Mobilisation and Recruitment: The SSPM/A has called on the people of South Sudan to join the wagon of the second liberation, and thousands of the oppressed and marginalised have risen to join the SSPM/A, proving that the will of the people cannot be silenced.
Phase-2: Organisation and Training: Discipline has been forged, unity strengthened, and our forces have become a living embodiment of resilience. This process continues, shaping us into a formidable army in the liberation struggle.

Phase-3: Readiness for Confrontation: For the past four years, we endured without logistics, yet we persevered. Now, we are equipped and prepared. The SSPM/A is no longer an online movement or Movement of words as vilified by the regime; it is now a force with teeth, ready to bite when the moment arrives. Our mission is not to seek revenge or positions, but to dismantle dictatorship, end corruption and tribalism, and build a NEW SOUTH SUDAN where justice, equality, dignity and democratic principles are the foundation of governance. We struggle not for division, but for unity with the national agenda. We sacrifice not for personal gain, but for the collective freedom of our people.

The Juba regime has wilfully deceived both the people of South Sudan and the international community by proclaiming its intention to hold elections in December 2026. Such pronouncements are nothing more than a calculated façade. It is legally and practically untenable to claim that genuine, credible, and democratic elections can be organised within seven months when the fundamental prerequisites remain wholly unmet. These include:

• The absence of adequate funding and logistical preparation;

• The lack of a permanent constitution to serve as the supreme legal framework;

• The failure to conduct a national census and delineate electoral boundaries;

• The non-repatriation of South Sudanese refugees, thereby disenfranchising a significant portion of the citizenry;

• The persistence of rampant insecurity across the country, which gravely undermines the free exercise of political rights.

• The immediate and unconditional release of all political detainees is a fundamental prerequisite for the creation of open and inclusive political and civic spaces, which are indispensable for fostering a conducive atmosphere in which genuine, free, fair, and credible elections can be conducted.
Considering these deficiencies, the regime's electoral rhetoric is nothing more than a stratagem to secure yet another illegitimate extension of its tenure, with the clear intention of clinging to power indefinitely. Such conduct constitutes a violation of both domestic constitutional obligations and international democratic norms.

The regime has further demonstrated its contempt for legality and peace by deliberately undermining the 2018 Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS), by arresting and silencing opposition leaders with the intention of eliminating any credible challengers to the ruling SPLM party. 

This constitutes a direct breach of the Agreement, a violation of international commitments, and an assault on the principle of political pluralism enshrined in democratic governance. Such actions not only erode the legitimacy of the electoral process but also amount to bad faith in the implementation of peace accords, thereby exposing the regime to international censure and potential legal consequences under regional and international law.

The regime's manoeuvres are neither democratic nor lawful; they are a calculated attempt to perpetuate authoritarian rule under the guise of constitutionalism. 

The people of South Sudan, together with the international community, must recognise these tactics for what they are, which is A DELIBERATE SUBVERSION OF PEACE, JUSTICE, AND DEMOCRACY.

We urge the people of South Sudan to join the SSPM/A/UPA to liberate themselves from the dictatorship and to endure with courage. Our struggle is not against peace, but against oppression, corruption, marginalisation, tribalism and injustice. We seek solidarity, not isolation. We seek justice, not chaos.

We urge our gallant forces to remain steadfast, disciplined and loyal. The Struggle demands SACRIFICE, but victory demands UNITY.
The SSPM/A and other opposition forces under the umbrella of the United People Alliance (UPA) are ready and committed to rescue the people of South Sudan from the dictatorial rule by all necessary means possible.

Long live the SSPM/A!
Long Live the UPA!
Long live the People

Gen. Stephen Buay Rolnyang
Chairman and Commander-in-chief, SSPM/A, SSPM/A MOBILE HEADQUARTERS.

The Watchdog Press—Watching your future

BREAKING: SA reaches another aviation safety milestone

South Africa reached another aviation safety milestone, achieving a preliminary result of 95.12% following an audit conducted by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

The ICAO Coordinated Validation Mission (ICVM) is an onsite follow up activity by the United Nations' specialised agency to assess a State's progress since its previous safety audit.

In South Africa's case, the last full scope audit was conducted in 2023, resulting in a 91.23% rating.
A final detailed report is expected from ICAO over the next 90 days.

This achievement reinforces confidence in South Africa's aviation system among international partners, airlines, investors and the travelling public.

It is also testament of the commitment of the entire aviation industry to regulatory compliance and continuous improvement.

By Angelo Akook L. Achuil, Law Student at the University of Juba

The recent reinstatement of General Gregory Vasili, better known as Deng Kuach Aduol, as Undersecretary of the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs is not just a political misstep; it is a deliberate act of sabotage against the South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF). Let us be blunt: Gregory is not a patriot. He is a predator in uniform. During his previous tenure as Undersecretary, he systematically drained the defence budget, with corruption so brazen that it directly cost the lives of South Sudanese soldiers. The most glaring example? The military operation against rebels in Jonglei State. Funds earmarked for logistics—fuel, food, ammunition, and medical supplies—were deliberately diverted by Gregory into private pockets. The result was catastrophic. In Pajut, government forces were not defeated in a fair fight; they were butchered because they had no supplies. The message to every soldier in the SSPDF is clear: your sacrifice means nothing next to the greed of a well-connected general. Morale is already shattered. Loyalty is turning into resentment. With Gregory back, the collapse of the SSPDF is not a threat; it is a timeline. And the failure of the South Sudanese government is no longer at the doorstep—it has already walked in. Please lay down your arms and go back home and look after your families, for this government does not value your sacrifice.

Amb. Ajing Deng Ajing's Case Adjourned Amid Panel Incompleteness and Judicial Engagement

The Supreme Court of South Sudan has formally adjourned proceedings in the matter of Ajing Deng Ajing to May 7, 2026, due to the court's inability to constitute a full bench for the scheduled sitting on April 30, 2026. 

According to court officials, the adjournment arose from the engagement of the Chief Justice in official duties at the Presidency, thereby rendering the panel incomplete and procedurally unable to proceed with the hearing.

Ajing Deng Ajing, a former Executive Director in the Office of the President, remains in detention for a prolonged period without the institution of formal charges. His legal counsel has challenged the legality of the continued detention, contending that it constitutes a violation of due process and applicable legal safeguards, and has petitioned the Court for appropriate judicial intervention.

The adjourned session is expected to proceed with the defence team’s submission of their legal responses, as the matter advances within the Court’s adjudicative framework.

SPLM Insider Buzz: Secretary-General Dr. Akol Paul Koordit's Quiet Power Play Many People Don’t Know

Word on the ground in Juba is that Dr. Akol Paul Kordit, the SPLM Secretary General, is working overtime to sweet-talk President Kiir into shaking up the ruling party SPLM Political Bureau. He is not being blatant about it—no fiery speeches or public spats, but he is been dropping hints in private meetings, pushing for the removal of a few big names who have been thorns in his side.

Sources close to SG Akol say he is genuinely spooked by Chairman Salva Kiir's health. "Anything could happen anytime," he is been whispering to his inner circle, the kind of guys who grab coffee with him at the Secretariat and other private hangout corners. His angle? 

Clear the deck now, sidelining rivals indirectly so that if the worst happens to Kiir, then SG Akol would be positioned to step up without a messy scrum. It is classic backroom manoeuvring, framing it as "streamlining the Political Bureau for unity" while really carving out space for himself, while misinforming many people that he is doing what the Chairman, Salva Kiir, has asked to be done. Names floating around removal in the Political Bureau include some heavy hitters who he described as having clashed with him before, though no one is spilling full details yet.

This could stir up real drama in the ruling SPLM Party ranks, especially with elections on the horizon. SG Akol is playing it smart, but if it leaks wider, expect pushback. SG Akol being too ambitious thinks selling those who have criticized President Kiir would fool the Chairman – President Kiir to accept to dismiss the people he recommends. 

On the sidelines of his meeting with his circle, SG Akol believes the likes of Kuol Manyang, James Wani Igga and Daniel Awet Akot are too old and not even effective in discussing the party's stressful affairs and that they are not the people he is worried about at this stage of internal crisis.

The following people are Akol's targets in the political bureau:

1. Tut Gatluak Manime
2. Paul Mayom Akech
3. Nhial Deng Nhial 
4. Awut Deng Achuil
5. Jemma Nunu Kumba 
6. Peter Lam Both
7. Rin Tueny Mabor
8. Louis Lobong Lojore
9. Stephen Dhieu Dau 

SG Akol has already engineered an agreement with his personal friends within the security sector to let him be secretly helped by framing and detaining individuals he perceives as saboteurs to his underground agenda. 

The Watchdog Press – Watching Your Future

———————For Public Education———————

The constitution of the South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority (SSCAA) explicitly defines the roles and responsibilities of SSCAA, without any conflict of interest with the Minister or Undersecretary. 

The Minister, Hon. Rizik appears intent on violating the SSCAA provisions for personal interests. 

Under the law, the Director General of the SSCAA has the mandate to appoint, reassign, and dismiss employees as illustrated below; 

• Section 19 (Functions and the Powers of the DG of SSSCA.

   Section 19 clearly stipulated the operational powers of the DG of SSCAA, which include regulating civil aviation, overseeing safety, licensing, and in many cases the administrative authority of the Director General, including managing staff.

• Section 22 (Appointment and Terms of Staff or Leadership of DG SSCAA. 

    
This section explicitly details how the Director General appoints Senior officials and their qualifications, and tenure in line with the ICAO principles.

• Section 26 (Administration, and Staff Management): 

  Explicitly explain how internal administration operations, surrounding employment matters such as recruitment, reassignment, disciplinary procedures, and dismissal of staff within the South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority are done by the DG. 

Basically, the ongoing arguments by slayqueens of Akuac Wol are centered on Dinka Riel Nhom Sakit, which has become the focal point of public servants' mismatch in the government institutions.

So, Hon. Rizik Hassan doesn't know what his roles are. He is gambling and should be taken back to his previous docket, the Ministry of Wildlife Conservation and Tourism to sell the snakes and lion calves to China. 

Now, where do those of AKUAC WOL and other constitutional gamblers draw their arguments if not Jiengism, Nyinrielism, and Nhomrielism? 

To this point, Dr. Ayiei Garang is right. Let the daughter of the veteran, an aviation specialist, Amel Ajong, carry on with her duties.

Clarification on the circulating names of 13 individuals identified by the National Security Service to be behind the 211 Sentry Facebook page

Watchdog Press management conducted a thorough investigation and found out that among those identified 13 people, two persons (number 3 Captain Dut Lual Anei and number 5 John De Mayuek in the list) are innocent. They are not part of the 211 Sentry Facebook page. Therefore, we are very sorry for having published untrue information which incorrectly linked them to this dangerous Facebook page. We also received new messages which show more individuals are participating in subversive activities of this 211 Sentry page.

text:
Update on the reported appointments involving Deputy First Lady Gregory Vasily and his daughter, Marina Ayen Gregory Vasily Dimitri for their different top positions in the Government of South Sudan

Recent developments in Juba, South Sudan, have raised serious concerns regarding the ongoing internal maneuvering and irregular appointment processes at the highest levels of government. According to emerging reports from reliable eyewitnesses, a few days ago Deputy First Lady Gregory Vasily, his daughter Marina Ayen Gregory, and Presidential Executive Director James Deng Wal secretly held a closed-door meeting. During this meeting, they are said to have discussed an attempt to forge a presidential decree that would appoint Gregory Deng Kuac Aduol to the position of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) or Director General (DG) of the Internal Security Bureau (ISB). This secret move, reflects a troubling willingness to bypass formal state procedures for personal or political gain.

However, the plan encountered immediate resistance. Key officials within J1, including the Presidential Security Director and the Minister of Presidential Affairs, have strongly opposed the attempt. Their resistance appears to have exposed the risks associated with the planned forgery, ultimately forcing Marina Ayen and James Deng Wal to abandon their initial objective. This moment highlights the presence of internal checks within the system, even amid indications of misconduct.

Following the failure of the initial plan, an alternative arrangement was pursued. Gregory was instead appointed as Deputy Director General of the General Intelligence Bureau (GIB), also known as External Security Services, a branch of the National Security Service of South Sudan. Reports indicate that the appointment letter was drafted and issued with what is described as a digitalized presidential approval. Despite receiving the letter, Gregory angrily reacted with dissatisfaction, viewing the role as significantly below his expectations. His response has seriously escalated into a tense confrontation with Marina Ayen and James Deng Wal, underscoring internal divisions and frustration over unmet ambitions.

During this confrontation, Marina and Deng are said to have pleaded for more time, assuring Gregory that they would work to remove officials within J1 who had opposed his elevation to more powerful positions such as CDF or DG of ISB. This new strategy suggests a broader effort to restructure key decision-making positions within J1 in order to create space for future influence, a move which is raising further concerns about governance integrity and institutional stability.

The situation became more complicated when Marina Ayen was unexpectedly removed from her position following official charges of her involvement in the theft of over 1.5 million USD from the President’s secured funds. Her removal marked a turning point, triggering open conflict between her and President’s ED James Deng Wal, whom she directly accused of failing to protect her during the conflict of stolen money of the President. This fallout not only weakened their alliance but also intensified the broader power struggle surrounding Gregory’s ambitions and influence in the corners of J1.

At the same time, Marina Ayen and her allies strategically shifted their focus toward confronting ED James Deng Wal directly. Facing mounting pressure from multiple fronts, Deng Wal seen to have moved quickly to stabilize his position by coordinating with the Minister of Presidential Affairs. In response, Marina Ayen was offered a position as Deputy Managing Director of NILEPET. However, she aggressively rejected the offer, dismissing it as inadequate and instead openly declaring her intention to return to J1 in a more influential role—specifically aiming to replace James Deng Wal as Executive Director. Sources said Marina Ayen’s bid for ED position is fully backed by her auntie the First Lady Mary Ayen Mayardit. 

Similarly, Deputy First Lady Gregory has also angrily refused to accept his re-appointment as Deputy Director General of the General Intelligence Bureau. His ally Achan Agoth told someone that Gregory have insisted that his expectations were firmly set on either the CDF or DG of ISB positions, and that he is unwilling to settle for what he perceives as a lesser role. His stance reflects a broader theme of political ambition and dissatisfaction within elite circles, further fueling tensions. This rejection of position has proved that Gregory sees this Government as a family property not the Government of the 64 tribes of South Sudan. 

Despite his initial rejection, there are indications that Gregory may ultimately reconsider his position. Sources suggest that close family members, including his sister the First Lady Mary Ayendit, have advised him to accept the re-appointment in order to avoid potential conflict with President Salva Kiir Mayardit, who is also his brother-in-law. This perspective emphasizes the delicate balance between personal relationships and political decisions within the leadership structure.

As it stands, Deputy First Lady Gregory is expected to assume office as Deputy Director General of the General Intelligence Bureau in the coming days, although this remains subject to change. Meanwhile, there are growing indications that Marina Ayen may still be positioning herself for a return to J1, potentially as a replacement for ED James Deng Wal. These ongoing developments point to a fluid and highly contested political environment. It is unpredictable that Marina Ayen will win the ED position since there are other influential figures such as Dr. Santino Matiok Akuei, Hon. Atak Santino Majak and General Joseph Anyak Lual eyeing on the same seat.

More updates will follow as the situation continues to unfold. Stay informed for the latest developments.

Source: Pakaal Insightfulnews

The Greed of Deputy First Lady Gregory Has Created a Dangerous Crisis in the Juba Regime’s Traditional Succession Plan Which is Unexpectedly Taking Long to be Implemented as Planned 

The greed of Deputy First Lady Gregory has blindly caused a serious crisis within the Juba regime’s traditional succession arrangement. Through his reckless recommendations, he has placed the regime’s succession plan in significant jeopardy.

He is widely seen as the political architect behind divisive and troubling decisions, including the detention of individuals at the Blue House. Although these cases are publicly linked to corruption allegations, the arrests appear to be driven more by suspicions that certain individuals could undermine the agreed-upon succession plan. This plan, reportedly supported by President Kiir and his close allies, seeks to position Adut as a successor to the current leadership.

Deputy First Lady Gregory advanced the idea that several individuals should be arrested under accusations of financial mismanagement, particularly related to oil revenues. These actions were justified on the grounds that such individuals might sabotage the succession arrangement. As a result, their detention was intended to ensure the smooth implementation of this controversial plan.

After formulating this strategy, he mobilized influential figures from various political factions to pressure President Salva Kiir Mayardit, who ultimately authorized the arrests.

This situation raises grave concerns. It suggests that some detainees may eventually be released under strict conditions, while others could face prolonged imprisonment or even risk losing their lives in detention, especially if the succession process drags on due to emerging challenges.

To President Salva Kiir Mayardit:
On what legal and constitutional grounds were these arrests authorized, and how do they align with the rule of law and human rights protections in South Sudan?

To United Nations and the broader international community:

What concrete steps will you take to investigate these politically motivated detentions and ensure accountability for potential human rights violations?

To both the South Sudanese leadership and international stakeholders:

How can a legitimate and peaceful succession process be guaranteed if it is enforced through intimidation, detention, and suppression of perceived political opponents?

The Watchdog Press – Watching Your Future

Lawyers representing Benjamin Bol Mel have rejected a demand from the Ministry of Justice of South Sudan to issue an apology, saying their actions were lawful and justified.

In a letter submitted on April 7, the legal team from Kiirdit & Co. Advocates argued that the ministry’s response to their earlier court motion lacked legal backing and did not cite any relevant laws.

The lawyers also denied accusations that they leaked the case documents to the media. They said media houses obtained the information independently and that informing the public is protected under the law.

On the issue of detention, the lawyers maintained that holding someone for more than 24 hours without court approval is unconstitutional and can be challenged publicly demanding answers why their client Benjamin Bol Mel continues to be detained without charges.

They further stated that the Justice Ministry has no authority to demand an apology from them, arguing that lawyers are only accountable to the South Sudan Bar Association on professional matters.

In conclusion, the lawyers said they have done nothing wrong and will not apologize, insisting their actions were aimed at protecting their client’s rights and ensuring due process.

𝗕𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱

The dispute began after lawyers for Benjamin Bol Mel filed a legal challenge against his detention.

In response, the Ministry of Justice of South Sudan accused them of misconduct, including leaking documents and using improper language, and asked them to submit a written explanation and apology.

The lawyers’ latest response rejects those claims and escalates the standoff into a broader legal dispute.

Here is the full quoted statement by Akoc Akuei Manhiem: “Rescuing South Sudan from the Brink of Collapse

An Appeal by Akoc Akuei Manhiem to His Excellency the President of the Republic of South Sudan

South Sudan stands at the precipice, staring into the abyss of collapse. The signs are unmistakable: a crippling economic crisis, a peace agreement teetering on the edge, and rural villages plagued by insecurity that claims innocent lives. The government's deliberate struggle to pay its public servants, coupled with the threat of Iran's influence disrupting global trade routes, unpaid salaries, and diplomatic missions facing closure due to lack of funds, all point to a deeper malaise.

The SPLM's internal power struggle has reignited, birthing multiple leaders without a legacy to honor. We've created a system where messengers wield more power and wealth than their masters. The government's direction is increasingly unclear, with policies seemingly crafted to serve elite interests rather than the people.

Your Excellency, there is a need for you to pull up numerous honest, dedicated sons and daughters of South Sudan to guide his daily activities and rescue the country from collapse. I doubt the current establishment can shed its con artist network skin to become patriots advancing the country's interest.

Yet, hope remains. Your Excellency has opportunities to rewrite South Sudan's narrative, to pursue sustainable peace and development. I urge you to continue seeking solutions, for there are young people willing to defend South Sudan with their lives.

It's time for a paradigm shift. Leaders who prioritize people over personal gain. The world watches, and the people of South Sudan count on their leaders to act on peace, stability, and social services improvement.

Will we rise to the challenge and genuinely focus on helping our country, or will we let South Sudan collapse? The choice is ours.”
